Name: PAOTINSAT GUITE
Citation Details: On 30th November, 2020, a 24 hours’ special ambush party of Ghatak Team of 59 Bn, BSF led by Shri Paotinsat Guite, SI(GD), familiar with the terrain & enemy tactics, was deployed along with anticipated ingress route of the terrorists in highly sensitive Damaikush Bowl on LoC under Army Ops Control of 120 Inf Bde. 2. On 1st December 2020 at about 0835 hours, the Ghatak team was fired upon from close proximity of Ambush site from the direction of Damaikush Nullah (Pak Side). Shri Paotinsat Guite, SI(GD), displaying intrepid nerves of steel, took immediate control of situation, re-sitting the Ambush and coordinated effective, swift and aggressive retaliatory fire towards the terrorist group, despite the heavily mined terrain with undulating ground and thick vegetation. While manoeuvring to engage the enemy, Shri Paotinsat Guite, SI(GD), was shot through his upper torso. With total disregard for his own safety, he continued engaging the enemy under overwhelming fire in order to provide protective fore for his team. Despite being grievously wounded, he exhibited raw courage and successfully neutralized one of the terrorist. 3. Shri Paotinsat Guite, SI(GD), was evacuated amid heavy firing by enemy posts and terrorists through Infantry Safe Lane (ISL) where he was declared dead by Medical Officer, making the supreme sacrifice to thenation in the line of duty. 4. During the entire operation, the dynamic leadership of Shri Paotinsat Guite, SI(GD), which resulted in killing of three militants of Hizbul Mujahideeen. The conspicuous gallantry, intrepidity and herorism at the risk of his life above and beyond the call of duty and at the cost of his own life are in keeping with the highest traditions of the Force. Therefore, Shri Paotinsat Guite, SI(GD), is awarded of ‘Kirti Chakra’ (Posthumously).

Name: DAVID MANLUN
Biography: Kirti Chakra (Posthumous)/ 06 June 2017 Major David Manlun Major David Manlun was born on 27 July 1985 in Imphal, Manipur. A son of army veteran Subedar M. Khamzalam, he grew up in a family with deep military roots. He completed his schooling at Army Public School, Shillong, and graduated from St. Anthony’s College, Shillong, in 2006. With a passion for sports, music, and languages, Maj David was known for his vibrant personality, multilingual abilities, and leadership qualities. He joined the Officer Training Academy, Chennai, in 2009 and was commissioned into the 1st Battalion, the Naga Regiment in March 2010. After initial operational service in Naugam (J&K), he later served at Bakloh in Himachal Pradesh and was posted to Nagaland with 164 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) Naga in 2014. For his outstanding service, he was awarded the Chief of Army Staff Commendation on 15 August 2016. He was due to begin probation for the National Security Guard on 23 June 2017. On 06 June 2017, acting on intelligence inputs about militant presence in the Lappa area of Mon district, Nagaland, near the Myanmar border, Maj David led a joint operation involving Para commandos and his unit. During the mission, the team was engaged in a fierce encounter with militants from ULFA(I) and NSCN(K) outfits. Despite being under heavy fire, Major David led from the front, encouraging his troops and directing the assault. He was grievously injured during the firefight and was martyred. Inspired by his leadership, his troops continued the operation successfully, recovering a large cache of weapons and ammunition. For his gallantry, leadership, and supreme sacrifice in the face of grave danger, Major David Manlun was posthumously awarded the Kirti Chakra

Name: SANJEEV SINGH
Biography: 07 Sepoy Sanjeev Singh of the 18 DOGRA regiment served in the Indian Army with dedication and discipline. From 07 February to 09 February 1998 Sepoy Sanjeev Singh took part in an operation in the area of village Chamrer (Surankot Sector) in Jammu and Kashmir. Sepoy Sanjeev Singh was the scout of the column during the operation. As he approached a stretch of thick jungle he,, was fired upon by militants injuring him , critically. Despite bleeding profusely and under intense fire of automatic weapons, Sepoy Sanjeev Singh crawled, to a vantage point, from where he could fire effectively for his platoon to deploy. Unmindful of his safety, he rushed forward and pounched over a , militant who was firing continuously at the platoon end Killed the militant in close hand to hand combat. Sepoy Sanjeev Singh displayed indomitable courage and presence of mind in the face, of militant, fire. He despite being greviously wounded, continued to engage the militant's thus preventing casualties to his, platoon. He expired when being evacuated on 27 February 1998, a bullet lodged in his spine could not be removed. Sepoy Sanjeev. Singh displayed conspicuous gallantry, unparalleled tenacity, devotion to service beyond the call of duty and spirit of self sacrifice. Link :https://gallantryawards.gov.in/awardee/3342

Name: SANJIV KUMAR
Biography: Kirti Chakra (Posthumous) / 04 April 2020 Subedar Sanjiv Kumar, Kirti Chakra Subedar Sanjiv Kumar (JC-413798Y), of 4 PARA (Special Forces), Indian Army, hailed from village Dehra, Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh. Enrolled into the Parachute Regiment on 30 August 1996, he had served multiple tenures along the Line of Control and had also been part of the elite National Security Guard. On 04 April 2020, Subedar Sanjiv Kumar led a Special Forces detachment that was helidropped in the Keran Sector of Jammu and Kashmir to intercept infiltrating terrorists attempting to cross from Pakistan. After trekking for hours through waist-deep snow, the team tracked the movement of the infiltrators. As they approached the suspected location, two leading scouts fell into a nallah where the terrorists were hiding and came under heavy fire. Without hesitation, Subedar Sanjiv Kumar, along with his buddy, advanced into the nallah under intense fire to rescue the wounded scouts. While his buddy provided covering fire, he evacuated one injured scout to safety. He then moved forward again to rescue the second scout and came under a volley of gunfire. Displaying exemplary courage, he charged at the terrorists, neutralizing one at close range and engaging the others in fierce hand-to-hand combat, injuring two more before succumbing to a gunshot wound. His fearless leadership and indomitable spirit inspired his team to eliminate five hardcore terrorists in the ensuing encounter. Subedar Sanjiv Kumar’s gallantry, devotion to duty, and supreme sacrifice stand as a testament to the highest traditions of the Indian Army. For his exceptional courage, leadership, and ultimate sacrifice beyond the call of duty, Subedar Sanjiv Kumar was posthumously awarded the Kirti Chakra.

Name: AJIT V BHANDARKAR
Biography: Lieutenant Colonel Ajit Vasudev Bhandarkar was born on 31 December 1960 to Shri U V Bhandarkar and Smt Shakuntala V Bhandarkar in Wadala, Bombay. He was the youngest of the three siblings —the eldest being Col Arun Bhandarkar (Retd), a former Indian Army officer, and Anil Bhandarkar. Ajit, being the youngest among them, was a super active child. He would feel secure in the presence of his mother while his mother was busy with the household chores. Though it was a nuclear family, their home was always packed with relatives. 1 Lieutenant Colonel Ajit, SC as an infant, lying down with his brothers Col Arun Bhandarkar (Retd) to the left and Mr Anil Bhandarkar to the right. 1 The GAP team is deeply grateful to Mrs Shakuntala Ajit Bhandarkar for granting the GAP team permission to access and use content from her book “The Saga of a Braveheart: Lt Col Ajit V Bhandarkar Shaurya Chakra” published by Vij Books India (1 August 2021). No copyright infringement is intended and it is not intended to hurt anyone or make sales of any sort. All copyright belongs solely to the relevant author/publisher. In 1964, Shri U V Bhandarkar came back to Karnataka to start the new office of New India Assurance Company. The family stayed in the company accommodation at Rajajinagar. All the three siblings joined National English School, which is presently known as National Public School Rajajinagar, Bangalore. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit Vasudev Bhandarkar had shown keen interest in joining the Indian Army since his childhood. To assist him to achieve his childhood goal, he was mentored and counselled by Mrs Kusum Bhat, the Headmistress of the school. He was successful in clearing the entrance exam to join the Sainik School Bijapur. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit Vasudev Bhandarkar’s mother, too was very encouraging, cheered him to do his best and motivated him to follow his dream. Her two sons joined the Indian Armed Forces- Colonel Arun Bhandarkar joined the Corps of EME and her youngest son, Lieutenant Colonel Ajit Vasudev Bhandarkar joined the Infantry. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit belonged to a very close-knit family and the presence of his uncle, aunt and cousins would keep Ajit motivated and happy. As a student, he was very determined and focused and would want to give his best in whatever he did. His cousins, Pradeep Bhat, Deepak Bhat and Nivedita Bhat, were always there for him and a beautiful bond was formed, which continued even after the school days. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit, SC as a school student standing second row, first from left Apart from being excellent in his academics, Lieutenant Colonel Ajit was also the school cricket team captain. He played full back in football and hockey, and it was difficult to break his defence since he was so proficient in his skills. Apart from that, he also loved horse-riding, swimming and volley ball. Since he was also the School Captain, his team spirit and leadership qualities were gradually getting sharpened during his adolescence. He was so genuine and empathetic that his classmates called him ‘Manav’ in memory of the idealistic character role that cine star Dharmendra had played in the famous Hindi film Dost in 1974. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit, SC during his NDA days - G Sqn Group Photograph In 1978, Lieutenant Colonel Ajit cleared the UPSC exam and joined the 59 th course of the NDA as part of the Golf Squadron. He joined the 69th Course of the Indian Military Academy, Dehradun as Army Cadets in January 1981, after graduating from National Defence Academy. He was successfully commissioned into the 18 MADRAS unit on 19 December 1981 as 2 nd Lt. When 2nd Lt Ajit joined the battalion it was based in Tamze, Sikkim. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit unit later moved to Secunderabad in June 1982. Soon, there were fresh orders to move to Gandhinagar, Gujarat immediately. Gandhinagar was a peaceful station but the unit was always involved in some or the other operations, participating in military exercises or assisting local civil authorities when the internal security situation deteriorated. A group pic of 18 MADRAS (Mysore) unit officers: Lieutenant Colonel Ajit, SC standing third from left After his tenure in Gandhinagar, Lieutenant Colonel Ajit Vasudev Bhandarkar attended the Battalion Support Weapon Course (O)-37 from February 1987 to June 1987. He was posted to OTA as an Instructor on 26 November 1987 and was in charge of the Kohima company. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit, SC as DS at OTA (standing second row, second from left) As an instructor, he was a role model to many of his GCs. He would frequently have an informal chat with them and get to understand them. There were a few cadets who had come from a civilian background and had no knowledge about Army life and its tough training norms. They did feel intimidated by the strict regime and the exacting routine. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit would, like a good friend, explain to them the purpose behind the rigorous training schedule. As a Directing Staff (DS), he closely monitored and mentored each and every one like a father figure. He would closely keep an eye on the Cadets during the practice sessions, accompany them on their outdoor training and camps, and motivate each and everyone in the Kohima company to do their best. His company was adjudged the best passing out company of 48th SSC course. Later, Lieutenant Colonel Ajit did his Junior Command Course 53 from August 1988 to November 1988. While the Junior Command Course is for a Captain to become a Major and assume the responsibility of Company Commanders; Senior Command is for a Major to assume the appointment of Commanding Officer of an Infantry Battalion or equivalent units in other arms and services. Junior Command Course Ser 53 - Aug 1988: Lieutenant Colonel Ajit, SC standing second row, third from right By March 1990 Lieutenant Colonel Ajit was posted back to the unit which was located in Ferozepur, Punjab as a young Major. It was during his tenure at Ferozepur, he got married to Mrs Shakuntala Ajit Bhandarkar on 11 October 1990. He later joined the three-month Intelligence Course at the Military Intelligence School, Pune in April 1991. Ajit cleared the Defence Service Staff Course (DSSC), and attended the 49 th course in 1993-94. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit, SC at Ferozepur, with CO Col Kuppa (Ajit sitting second from left) After successfully completing his DSSC course, Major Ajit was posted as Brigade Major at Nathu La in East Sikkim district from June 1994 to May 1996. Later in May 1996, he was posted at the MS Branch at Army Headquarters in New Delhi. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit attended the Senior Command Course 80th batch from 08 December to 07 March 1998. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit, SC Standing last row, sixth from left during the Senior Command Course 80 - Mar 1998 On 05 June 1998 after being promoted to the rank of Lt Col, Ajit reported to 25 RR as a second in command which was based in Doda. In June 1999, 25 RR had moved from their location Bhaderwah (Doda Distt, J&K) to Surankote (Poonch Distt, J&K) in the thick of OP VIJAY. The battalion was continuously carrying out military operations in the area. Indian Union Territory (formerly State) of Jammu Kashmir is facing Low Intensity Conflict encompassing all kinds of armed conflicts below the threshold of war. These include proxy war, terrorism and insurgencies; border skirmishes also fall within this category. It involves protracted struggle of competing principles and ideologies. Pakistan is involved in a proxy war with India using non-state players to fight on their behalf across the country but primarily in Kashmir. Pakistan has been, since independence, aiding and abetting terrorism in the state of Jammu and Kashmir. The role Indian Army is mandated to safeguard National Interests from External Aggression and Internal Subversion. The Indian Army is committed to bringing down the levels of violence to "manageable levels" in Jammu and Kashmir so as to restore the confidence of the people and create a secure environment to facilitate smooth governance and socio economic development. Army’s focus is on conducting of surgical and professional operations based on hard intelligence, while cause minimum inconvenience to the local populace. Simultaneously, the focus has been on destruction of terrorist infrastructure, resulting in a large number of hideouts being busted and recovery of huge caches of arms and ammunition. 2 In the last one decade, the overall security situation in J&K has undergone an appreciable change and is well under control of the Security Forces. All parameters of proxy war are at an all-time low and the current situation indicates a shift towards normalcy and peace. The growing stability is indicative of the success of the untiring efforts of all Security Forces which includes the Army’s Counter Terrorist (CT) efforts. 3 The continuous employment of Army in Counter Insurgency duties along with existing conventional threat, warranted a specially structure and organised force to deal with India’s Internal Security situation. Rashtriya Rifles was raised on 01 October 1990 by then Chief of Army Staff General VN Sharma, PVSM, AVSM as the premier fighting force of Indian Army. The Force is engaged in constant counter terrorism operations. The Force has fully justified its deployment in Jammu and Kashmir by creating secure environment leading to incident free elections, carried out flood relief operations, impacted the quality of life of locals in addition to have been involved in continuous operations against terrorists. The personnel in Rashtriya Rifles units come on deputation from all arms and services of Indian Army. Till 2017, the units of Rashtriya Rifles have repeatedly proved their mettle and have earned 7 Ashok Chakras, 34 Kirti Chakras, 238 Shaurya Chakras, 1637 Sena Medals and 67 Chief of Army Staff Unit Counter Terrorist Operations in Jammu and Kashmir, Indian Army https://indianarmy.nic.in/KnowYourArmy/knowyour-army-main/counter-terrorist-operations-in-jammu-and-kashmir-operations-un-mission 2 3 Ministry of Defence, Government of India, Annual Report 2009-10 https://mod.gov.in/sites/default/files/AR910.pdf Citations. 4 Lieutenant Colonel Ajit Vasudev Bhandarkar as a second in command of 25 RR was meticulously chalking out his strategies for his troops and studying terrorist activity so that the paltan could eliminate the terrorists who were trying to instil fear in the minds of the people and disrupt peace in the beautiful valley. Since 25 RR was a newly raised unit, Lieutenant Colonel Ajit travelled to Delhi to purchase some basic sports equipment for troops to ensure their physical fitness as they worked in high altitudes. Team games like volleyball, basketball, etc. were played in the evening and also intercompany matches brought a lot of cheer and josh to the troops. He was always working for the welfare of his troops and simultaneously scheming to neutralise terrorists in his area. He used to visit all company/ platoon posts and developed a firsthand understanding of terrain, insurgent network and intelligence set up our Battalion had created in its Area of Responsibility (AoR). He had an uncanny knack of connecting with people of all hues and colours. The youngsters watched him both with awe and pride. His humility, straight-talk, fearlessness and solicitude simply qualified him to be a role model for the younger generation. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit, SC with his hands at the back, briefing his team 27th Raising Day Rashtriya Rifles, Press Information Bureau, Government of India, Ministry of Defence https://pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=171314 4 On the morning of 30 October,1999 after attending the monthly regular Commanding Officers conference at the sector headquarters, the COs were informed about some terrorists trying to enter the Indian territory in the Surankot area. The CO on his return to the unit, during his meeting with the unit officers, informed them about the inputs he had gathered about the terrorists trying to enter Indian soil. The CO discussed the details with his officers on the future course of action. Lieutenant Colonel Ajit Vasudev Bhandarkar, after discussion with the CO, volunteered to lead the QRT team. He made detailed plans, organised his team with manpower, weapons, ammunition. He briefed his team and also made logistic preparation and considered several contingency plans. The team was all set and proceeded on its mission, in the evening. The operations commenced; Sepoy Binu, his buddy, was in front of him, and Havildar Shiva Kumar another buddy was at the back, and he was behind the leading element of the QRT. It enabled him to exercise command and control over the entire team and he was giving the necessary instructions to the team. They were going for a search operation to eliminate five hardcore terrorists hiding in the border village. All of a sudden, Ajit spotted the terrorists escaping towards the Nullah. He started chasing them and shot dead one of them at point-blank range. The second terrorist was hiding behind the Nullah and was firing indiscriminately, injuring Ajit and also his buddy, Sepoy Binu grievously. While his buddy fell unconscious, he moved and lobbed a grenade at the terrorists. He then crawled forward and shot down one more terrorist. Thus, Ajit eliminated three hardcore terrorists, however, he also had taken a bullet on his forehead, just below his helmet and also got multiple splinter injuries on his right forearm. He displayed gallantry and bold leadership utterly unmindful of danger by leading from the front in the true spirit of his Regiment. The President of India awarded Lieutenant Colonel Ajit Vasudev Bhandarkar Shaurya Chakra, posthumously on 12th October 2001. This was the first time in the history of 25 RR, a senior officer was killed in action and was awarded a gallantry award. The family of Lieutenant Colonel Ajit moved to Bangalore. After Lieutenant Colonel Ajit passed away, Mrs Shakuntala Ajit Bhandarkar took on the role of both the father and mother. Their elder son Nirbhay joined his dad’s own unit, the Marauders 18 MADRAS (Mysore) after completing his graduation from Christ University and training in the prestigious OTA, Chennai. Akshay, the younger son, cleared the NDA written exam, after completing his 12th Board exam, and also the CET of Karnataka. He decided to pursue his undergrads in Engineering from PES university, Bengaluru. Akshay is now a Submariner in the Indian Navy.. Name: VARSI VASUDEV RAO
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous) / 13 August 1994 https://gallantryawards.gov.in/awardee/2198 On 13th August 1994 in a village in Thoubal district in Manipur, a column was tasked to seek and destroy Naga militants. Naik Rao was leader of the leading section, when they reached the village, they were fired upon by the militants hiding in the college complex. Naik Rao and his men returned the fire. However, he was hit by a bullet in his chest, Bleeding profusely he led his men with extreme courage and total disregard to his own safety, till he breathed his last, This supreme sacrifice of his galvanized his column into action and the operation resulted in subsequent killing of nine militants and apprehension of one of them. Naik Varsi Vasudev Rao, displayed exemplary courage, firm determination and devotion to duty at the cost of his own life.

Name: RAVINDRA KASHINATH NAITAM
Citation Details: On 12/11/2021, information was received about the gathering of armed members of Communist Party of India (CPI) (Maoist) group, numbering roughly 120-130 heavily armed insurgents and they planned to conduct a major attack on security forces in the backdrop of PLGA week. As per the orders and under the supervision of Shri Ankit Goyal, SP, Gadchiroli, an anti-naxal operation was chalked out by Shri Somay Munde, Addl. Supdt. of Police (Ops.), Gadchiroli. Based on this plan, an operation was launched involving 15 C60 parties led by Shri Somay Munde, Addl SP (Ops). As per the plan, the operational parties were divided into three group. On 12/11/2021 during the nocturnal hours, the first group led by Shri Somay Munde and another five officers and 137 policemen and the second group composed of seven officers and 110 policemen set out from Gadchiroli and were dropped via vehicle 8 km from the target area. Employing utmost stealth and speed both groups covered the said distance on moonless cloudy night trough hilly and densely forested area within 5 hours under cover of darkness. They reached the forest of Alondi on 13/11/2021 early in the morning. Similarly, the third group consisting of one officer and 85 men set out from AOP Kotgul at midnight of 12-13/11/2021 and reached the target area early in the morning. Thereafter all the three groups together began to comb through the forest. On 13/11/2021 at around 0600 hrs to 0630 hrs, while combing through the forest of Mardintola, the Maoists hidden on the hilltop, suddenly attacked the second group by opening indiscriminate fire. The commandos managed to shield themselves behind the trees and rocks and shouted out in appeal to the Maoists to stop gunfire and surrender. But the Maoists continued to fire at the commandos. The commandos of the second group retaliated at the direction of the Maoists by opening controlled fire. As the police pressure mounted, the Maoists fled into the thick forest. As the gunfire was heard by Shri Somay Munde, he immediately established coordinating among all the three groups through walkie-talkie sets and identified the direction in which Maoists fled. Shri Somay Munde chalked out a plan and thereafter began to chase the Maoists. As the commandos reached the near a hill, 90-100 armed Maoists hidden on the hilltop again attacked the commandos by opening accurate and devastating fire. During this exchange of fire, Shri Tikaram Katenge received grievous bullet injuries on the right hand and right shoulder. Due to bullet injuries to his right hand, his dominant hand was incapacitated and heavily bleeding. Sensing grave danger to his colleagues, in spite of grievous injuries, he shifted his rifle position to left hand and continued to retaliate. His unexpected counterattack caught three advancing naxals in surprise, during which he was able to neutralize all three Maoists armed with automatic weapons. In spite of fatal injuries, he continued to retaliate and showed conspicuous bravery. His counterattack encouraged his fellow commandos to retaliate aggressively in spite of being pinned down. He kept presence of mind in spite of bleeding heavily and fought pitched battle with the enemy merely 20 meters away. Through his gallant act, he was able to prevent further loss not only to his person but also to his buddies. But Maoists, seeing wounded jawans, began to encircle them in order to kill and snatch away the weapons of jawans. Maoists were using accurate BGL fire in order cause maximum damage. Due to growing pressure and heavy fire, the trapped men radioed Shri Somay Munde for immediate assistance. Shri Somay Munde directed his section to provide cover fire while he along with 6 men left their cover and began crawling to the spot under heavy fire. His assault group achieved a dominating position to lay accurate fire on the Maoists. Through controlled and accurate use of area weapons and automatic fire, he and his assault group neutralized six heavily armed Maoists. Further, in order to take advantage of this momentum to break the encirclement, he along with his buddy Shri Ravindra Naitam charged at the remaining Maoists in spite of a volley of bullets flying around. He and Shri Ravidnra Naitam laid down accurate fire to neutralize three more Maoists in order to save wounded jawans from imminent danger. The Maoists continued to fire indiscriminately at the commandos. Due to the excessive bleeding from the hand of injured Shri Tikaram Katenge, it was urgently required to evacuate him for immediate medical attention. Shri Munde formed a small group of commandos and sent them to identify a suitable place for helicopter landing for CASEVAC. While this group was moving along the edge of a hill, 20-25 armed Maoists suddenly attacked the group. After some time, the Maoists began flanking the group from different sides in order to lay fire from various directions at the jawans. Immediately, one of the commando informed Shri Munde over a walkie-talkie set about the encirclement of the Maoists and called for assistance. Sensing grave danger to his men, Shri Munde along with his group started moving towards the exchange of fire from the right direction. Meanwhile, he directed the third group to rush towards the exchange of fire from the left direction. This coordinated flanking movement ensured that Maoists were outflanked. During this flanking maneuver, two Maoists hiding in the nearby bush fired indiscriminately at the flanking jawans in order to achieve surprise. Shri Ravindra Naitam, who was pilot of one of the sections, through presence of mind and utmost alertness identified the two hidden Maoists firing from the automatic weapon. With utter disregard for personal safety, he charged at the two Maoists and silenced them. During this charge, he received a grazing bullet wound to his head. In spite of shock and bleeding due to the bullet wound, he continued to fire in order to maintain pressure. His presence of mind and alertness ensured that his fellow jawans were saved from two Maoists in near-perfect ambush position. Meanwhile, seeing his wounded buddy n imminent danger from other Maoists, Shri Munde, with utter disregard for personal safety, left his cover and charged ahead and laid down cover-fire in order to achieve fire superiority. This surprise counter-attack by Shri Munde stunned advancing belligenrets. Through spot-on tactical acumen and audacious manuever, he was able to neutralise two more armed Maoists. This sudden counter attack destroyed morale among the Maoists rank, due to which they retreated from the wounded jawan. Due to this, other jawans were able to pull wounded Shri Ravindra Naitam to safety. Due to the coordinated attack of the commandos from both the sides, the Maoists began to retreat. Hence, the trapped commandos could be rescued successfully. During the search, police found 26 Maoists including women lying unconscious on the ground. Also 29, firearms and other naxal belonging in huge quantities were recovered from the place of incident. Importantly numerous shells of spent BGL were testimony to the amount of firepower used by the Maoists during exchange of fire. Further, a search operation on 16/11/21 led to discovery of another body along with a firearm. In recognition of extraordinary courage displayed by the police personnel, Shri Ravindra Naitam, Police Naik, is awarded of SHAURYA CHAKRA

Name: VIJAY SINGH
Biography: Major Vijay Singh, son of Shri Sher Singh, from District Jammu, Jammu and Kashmir, was a commissioned officer of the Jammu and Kashmir Rifles Regiment of the Indian Army. A resolute and professionally accomplished officer, he exemplified the regiment’s enduring ethos of discipline, leadership, and battlefield composure under pressure. On 15 May 1980, his battalion was deployed to counter hostile activity in the Imphal area. The next day, 16 May 1980, Major Vijay Singh led a patrol party on a reconnaissance mission. During the operation, a jeep approaching from the opposite direction suddenly opened fire on the patrol. Reacting with exceptional presence of mind, he returned fire and shot the armed occupant in the front seat. Without hesitation, he deboarded his vehicle, rallied his men, and directed them to take positions under fire. In the exchange that followed, all three militants were killed, and their jeep with arms and ammunition was recovered. One of the slain men was later identified as a wanted criminal involved in several robbery cases. Major Vijay Singh’s courage, quick decision-making, and effective leadership ensured mission success and the safety of his troops. For his exemplary bravery and devotion to duty, he was awarded the Shaurya Chakra on 26 January 1981.

Name: ABHISHEK SINGH
Citation Details: 06 - 07 January 2022 Major Abhishek Singh since joining battalion has exhibited exceptional resoluteness and leadership qualities taking part in four successful operations resulting in elimination of nine terrorists. On 06-07 January 2022, he was part of Operation Zoiu leading his team to lay initial cordon in Budgam District (Jammu and Kashmir). The alert officer observed suspicious movement of three individuals who opened indiscriminate fire on being challenged. Effective retaliation foiled escape bid. Post neutralisation of first terrorist, remaining two terrorists got holed up in narrow alley between houses. Major Abhishek Singh leading search team volunteered to clear it physically. While closing in team was fired upon by hiding terrorist and in ensuing firefight Major Abhishek Singh injured second terrorist with effective fire. Meanwhile grenade lobbed by third terrorist injured officer near left eye. Though bleeding profusely, officer regained his wit and located third terrorist firing onto search team. Appreciating grave danger to his buddy and disregarding personal safety the officer swiftly manoeuvred to acquire advantageous position and took aimed shots neutralising heavily armed category A+ foreign terrorist. For displaying commendable leadership and bravery thereby injuring one terrorist and eliminating another heavily armed foreign terrorist, Major Abhishek Singh is awarded of SHAURYA CHAKRA

Name: DEEPAK KUMAR PADDA
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous)/ 23 May 2005 Major Deepak Kumar Padda was born on 30 January 1976 in Hoshiarpur district in Punjab to Lieutenant Colonel Paras Ram, an army veteran and Smt Sharda Rani.1 He did his initial schooling from Kendriya Vidyalaya, Pathankot and later did his Bachelors in Science from DAV College, Chandigarh. Since his childhood Major Deepak Kumar Padda wanted to serve in the Armed Forces. He joined the Indian Army at the age of 23 after his training from the Indian Military Academy (IMA), Dehradun. Major Deepak Padda was commissioned in the 85 Armoured Regiment on 13 May 2000 at Mamun. He served with his parent unit for four years, and took part in various challenging operations. While in service he married Ms. Sonia Padda, and later they were blessed with a son Ritviek. Major Deepak Kumar Padda during his NDA days He was promoted to the rank of Captain in the year 2002, and as a young captain moved to Babina, Jhansi along with its unit in September 2003. He did his instructors course from Armoured Corps Centre and School, Ahmednagar, and later was sent on attachment with 14 GRENADIERS in 2004. He was promoted to the rank of Major in the same year. 85 Armoured Regiment was raised on 01 October 1976 by Late Lt Col DP Singh (Ex 63 CAV and 66 Armd Regt) at Vijay Lines, Ahmednagar. The Regiment on raising was equipped with Vijayanta Tanks. The forbearers of ‘85’ comprised of valiant officers from thirteen Armoured Regiments and gallant men from the Armoured Corps and the Regiment of Artillery. On the other hand, the GRENADIERS is an infantry regiment of the Indian Army with a rich and illustrious history. On 01 October 1943, one of the existing Infantry Division of Eastern Army, the 14 1 @ The GAP team is deeply grateful to Mrs. Sonia Padda for providing us with documents, information, and photographs of Major Deepak Kumar Padda, SC. infantry Division that was located at Chhindwara, was reorganised as training Division to basically hold trained recruits and train them for two months in jungle warfare. For this purpose the Division has raised a few training Battalions. One of its training Battalion, the 34 training Unit was being shared by the GRENADIERS Regimental and 3 MADRAS. Subsequently the MADRAS Regimental started raising its own independent units. 34 Unit was redesignated as 14 BATALLION of the BOMBAY GRENADIERS. After Word War-II was over, the Battalion was de-mobilised on 01 April 1946. The Battalion was re-raised post- independence on 01 January 1965 at Nasirabad, as the 14th Battalion the Grenadiers under Major SRS Manhas. The battalion has participated in many operations since its raising including OP Rakshak from October 1994-May 1997 and from October 1998- May 1999. The battalion was again part of Operation Rakshak from July 2004- September 2007. Major Deepak Kumar Padda By 2005, Major Deepak Kumar Padda had put in around 05 years of service and had gained the fieldcraft skills required to be operation-ready officer. The same year, there were a discernible drop in infiltration from Pakistan since 2004. The assessed successful infiltration up to December 2005 had come down to 335. This reduction was because of counter measures adopted by the Army. However, the period during June - July 2005 witnessed an upsurge in infiltration attempts by terrorists, belying the claims by Pakistan of their efforts in curbing terrorism from their soil. The residual strength of the terrorists as well as their potential, in terms of weapons and related infrastructure shown a decline, placing the terrorists on the backfoot. The Army's strategy of 'Iron Fist in a Velvet Glove' paid rich dividends, since it focused on conduct of surgical and professional operations based on real time intelligence, which causes minimum inconvenience to the local populace.2 During the year 2005, 1,990 terrorist incidents occurred as compared to 2,565 incidents during the year 2004. 557 civilians were killed in the year 2005, compared to 707 last year. The number of Security Force personnel killed in the year 2005 was 189, compared to 281 in 2004. 917 terrorists were killed in the year 2005, compared to 976 during the previous year. 3 It was in the Kupwara district, which according under section 3 of the Armed Forces (Jammu & Kashmir) Special Powers Act, 1990 was notified as ‘disturbed’ area, where Major Deepak Kumar Padda was posted on attachment with 14 GRENADIERS during the operation Rakshak in 2005. Major Deepak Kumar Padda was commanding the A’coy of 14 Grenadier and the Company Operating Base was on Tangdhar road. Major Deepak Kumar Padda was the commander of the A’coy that executed an operation on 23 May 2005 in general area Rangwar, District Kupwara, Jammu & Kashmir. On receipt of an information, Major Deepak rushed to the target site. Displaying acute tactical acumen, he readjusted the team positions to counter the disadvantageous terrain and himself crawled ahead to effectively engage the terrorists. In the intense fire-fight, Commander of the neighbouring team got injured. To prevent his men sustain further scathing bullets, Major Deepak charged firing on to the terrorists. Unprepared, for this kind of bravery and ferociousness, the terrorists started firing indiscriminately, hitting Major Deepak in his abdomen. Meanwhile, Commander of one of the teams sustained a fatal injury as he eliminated one of the terrorists. Unable to accept this irreparable loss. Major Deepak crawled ahead, ignoring his near fatal bullet injury and exhibiting unprecedented gumption, fatally killed the second terrorist with effective fire. Major Padda was evacuated from the site of action, and later succumbed to his injuries on 04 June 2005 in Army Hospital. Major Deepak Kumar Padda is survived by his wife Mrs Sonia Padda and son Ritviek. A school in Daulatpur, Pathankot, Punjab has been named as Shaheed Major Deepak Kumar Padda Government Senior Secondary School in his honour. Unable to accept this irreparable loss, Major Deepak crawled ahead, ignoring his near fatal bullet injury and exhibiting unprecedented gumption, fatally killed the second terrorist with effective fire. Major Padda was evacuated from the site of action and later he succumbed to his injuries on 04 June 2005 in Army Hospital. Major Deepak Kumar Padda exhibited exemplary valour, sterling leadership and made the supreme sacrifice while fighting the terrorists. Gazette Notification number 36 -Pres/2006 dated March 18, 2006

Name: GOSAVI KUNAL MUNNAGIR
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous)/ 29 November 2016 Major Kunal Munnagir Gosavi Major Kunal Munnagir Gosavi hailed from Pandharpur in Solapur district, Maharashtra. An alumnus of Kavathekar High School and Brihan Maharashtra College of Commerce, Pune, Major Kunal always aspired to join the Indian Army. He fulfilled this dream by clearing the Combined Defence Services Examination and was commissioned into the 166 Medium Regiment of the Regiment of Artillery in 2006. He later married Uma, and the couple had a daughter, Umang. Between 2013 and 2014, he served in Manipur, actively participating in counter-insurgency operations. In November 2016, while serving with 116 Medium Regiment in Nagrota, Jammu & Kashmir, Major Kunal responded to a deadly terror attack on the Army unit on 29 November 2016. At approximately 5:30 am, heavily armed militants stormed the Artillery unit, killing four soldiers and infiltrating residential buildings housing officers’ families and a mess. On being alerted, Major Kunal immediately activated the Quick Reaction Team (QRT) and led from the front. He swiftly evacuated injured personnel and family members to safety, cordoned off the area, and ensured containment of the terrorists within a limited zone. His leadership played a crucial role in preventing a massacre and protecting critical military assets. While bravely engaging the terrorists and guiding his troops, Major Kunal sustained a gunshot wound. Despite his injuries, he continued to command and guide the operation. He was later evacuated but succumbed to his injuries en route to the hospital. His actions not only stalled the terrorists' objective of hostage-taking but also confined the attack, minimizing further casualties. In this selfless act, Major Kunal Gosavi, along with six other brave soldiers, made the supreme sacrifice. For his unflinching courage, resolute leadership, and supreme sacrifice, Major Kunal Munnagir Gosavi was posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra.

Name: SUGATO SEN
Biography: Major Sugato Sen of 14 Assam, son of Sunil Kumar Sen and Uma Sen, hailed from Birbhum, West Bengal. On 26 March 1998 at 0940 hours, based on actionable intelligence that part of an action group of militants was hiding at village Pakihaga in Kokrajhar District of Assam, Major Sugato Sen, Officer Commanding 'C' Company, made a quick appreciation and decided to exploit the opportunity. Moving in broad daylight. Major Sugato Sen closed in and cot the hideout cordoned. Five militants rushed out of a hut firing at his team. Ordering the team to split in two. Major Sugato Sen along with two other ranks rushed towards two insurgents who were firing at them with automatic weapons. Unmindful of his personal safety, he fired and killed one militant on the spot. Thereafter, he guided and exhorted his team to complete the task providing covering fire. During the entire operation, Major Sugato Sen, led from the front which resulted in the killing of five hard core militants and recovery of four AK 56 Rifles along with ammunition. Major Sugato Sen displayed gallant act of valour, comradeship and dedication to duty with total disregard to personal safety. Link :https://gallantryawards.gov.in/awardee/326

Name: THAKUR SINGH
Biography: Sepoy Thakur Singh (later Havildar), was born in Borshi Rajputan village of Amritsar, Punjab. He was part of UN-Peacekeeping mission in Korea in the early 1950s and was awarded Ashok Chakra III, now Shaurya Chakra in recognition of his act of bravery and devotion to duty on 25 September 1953 while serving with Custodian Forces, India. Indian forces aided the UN Peacekeeping mission by providing army personnel for the Custodian Force under the Neutral Nations Repatriation Committee (NNRC) and Para Field Ambulance. The Custodian force was deployed to take control over the crisis situation related to the prisoners of war. Officers from the Military Police detachment, a part of the CFI and NNRC HQ outside the complex of one PsOW camp at the DMZ. halting it | Research News, The Indian Express 2 During the war the Indian contingent had to deal with a peculiar situation where the prisoners of war were not willing to go back to their respective countries. The CFI was commanded by Maj Gen S P P Thorat and the contingent comprised of 5 RAJ RIF, 6 JAT, 3 DOGRA, and 3 GARHWAL along with the support units of 190 Infantry Brigade. They were deployed to take charge of the prisoners of war (PsOW). The contingent had orders from the Indian government not to be a party to any confrontation or to engage in force, coercion, and violence against PsOW. Allowances were only made for minimum use of force but only for self-defense. The PsOW were interned in camps set up by the Indian forces, and were often called ‘CHIKEN RUNS’ by the American troops because of their resemblance to the chicken coops. Each of these enclosures were under the oversight and protection of an Indian commander. However, the task of handling the prisoners wasn’t a very easy one. The incidents of unrest and violence were frequently reported due to the tense circumstances, but the Custodian Forces of India remained determined to accomplish their duty to the best of their abilities and their management is still seen in a high regard. At one of the prison camps Sep Thakur Singh was on duty, as driver to the Deputy Commander, Custodian Force. He was standing near the gate and he saw the General Officer, Commanding Custodian force coming out of the camp with other senior officers after delivering a talk to the prisoners. Major B. S. Grewal, 8 DOGRA, who was working as a Chinese Interpreter, was the last to come out from the camp. Unfortunately, he was caught by a few rowdy prisoners and was forcibly dragged into the camp full of agitated PsOW. Sep Thakur Singh rushed to rescue him with complete disregard for his personal safety. The officer was being dragged from one tent to another but Sep Thakur Singh remained committed to saving the officer and was with him throughout, thus protecting him from serious injuries and facilitated his eventual rescue. 3
Citation Details: 6551869 Sepoy Thakur Singh ASC (25 Sep, 1953) On the 25th September 1953, the prisoners of war, approximately 24,000 in number, became truculent and started making rowdy demonstrations against the custodian Force, India. When the General Officer Commanding Custodian force was coming out of the camp with other senior officers after giving a talk to the prisoners, Major B. S. Grewal, 8 Dogra Regt., the Chinese Interpreter who was the last to come out, was forcibly dragged into the camp by the prisoners. Sepoy Thakur Singh, who was on duty as driver to the Deputy Commander, Custodian Force, and was standing near the gate, saw the officer being dragged into the camp by the rowdy prisoners and rushed to rescue him with complete disregard for his personal safety. The officer was being dragged from one tent to another but Sepoy Thakur Singh remained with him throughout and thus protected him from serious injury and facilitated his eventual rescue. Sepoy Thakur Singh’s magnificent example of devotion to duty and personal bravery were exemplary and reflected the highest tradition of the Army.

Name: SHRI MOHD. AKBAR
Biography: Head Constable Mohd Akbar served in the Jammu and Kashmir Police and was known as a committed and courageous policeman who discharged his duties with exceptional dedication under challenging operational conditions in the Kashmir Valley. On 19 April 2004, Head Constable Mohd Akbar was leading a police party assigned to provide security for a polling station in Lal Baba Sahib, Arampora, Sopore, in Baramulla district, ahead of the polling scheduled for 20 April 2004. As the security team was taking physical possession of the polling station complex and carrying out pre-election security arrangements, unidentified terrorists launched an attack by hurling a hand grenade into the premises. The grenade landed within the polling station complex, where police personnel and civilians were present, posing an immediate threat to many lives. Realising the grave danger without a moment's hesitation, Head Constable Mohd Akbar rushed towards the grenade. Fully aware of the risk involved, he picked it up with the intention of throwing it away from the polling station and in the direction from which the attack had originated. Before he could complete the action, the grenade exploded in his hands. The blast inflicted fatal injuries, and he was killed instantly. His selfless and courageous act absorbed the full impact of the explosion and prevented what could have been heavy casualties among the civilians and fellow police personnel assembled at the polling station. Through his extraordinary courage, presence of mind, and complete disregard for his own safety, Head Constable Mohd Akbar ensured the safety of many innocent lives. His actions reflected the highest traditions of the Jammu and Kashmir Police, exemplifying exceptional bravery, unwavering devotion to duty, and the ultimate sacrifice in the service of the nation. For this conspicuous gallantry, he was posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra, effective 19 April 2004.

Name: CHANDRA SINGH
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous)/ 25 November 2016 Naik Chandra Singh In November 2016, Naik Chandra Singh was deployed as part of a stop group during a Cordon and Search Operation in a village in Sopore district, Jammu and Kashmir. The target was a house sheltering two armed militants. During the operation, the militants opened heavy fire and hurled grenades in an attempt to break the security cordon and escape. One of the militants charged directly toward Naik Chandra Singh’s position, firing his weapon. In the ensuing gunfight, Naik Chandra Singh sustained grievous abdominal injuries. Despite his critical condition, he displayed exceptional courage and continued to engage the militant, understanding the imminent threat posed to his fellow soldiers. With unwavering determination and disregard for his own life, Naik Chandra Singh successfully neutralised the militant at close range, preventing a potential breakout and saving the lives of his comrades. He later succumbed to his injuries at the operation site. For his extraordinary bravery, presence of mind, and supreme sacrifice in the line of duty, Naik Chandra Singh was posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra.

Name: SANJAY KAUSHIK
Biography: Shaurya Chakra / 01 July 2009 On 01 July 2009 at 1300h, IC-46936F Lieutenant Colonel Sanjay Kaushik leading the Battalion Ghatak column, moved on reliable input about presence of four terrorists in house of a suspect at village Nilsu. On spot interrogation, provided input that the terrorists were likely to be hiding in the adjoining forest. The officer displayed tactical acumen by immediately resisting the cordon and coordinating a two pronged probe to locate terrorists in the forest which had dense foliage and steep slopes. On being probed, the terrorists fired on own parties spread along a nala, covered with big boulders and dense foliage. The fire fight continued in heavy rainstorm for approx two hours, when the officer anticipating approaching fading light, crawled forward from a flank against heavy fire and charged after throwing grenades. Disregarding personal safety, he closed in and killed two terrorists from point blank range and facilitated neutralization of the third terrorist. For this act of gallantry, he was awarded Shaurya Chakra on 26 Jan 2010.

Name: BHANDORIYA GOPALSINH MUNIMSINH
Biography: Vishisht Seva Medal Lance Naik Bhandoriya Gopalsinh Munimsinh Lance Naik Bhandoriya Gopalsinh Munimsinh hailed from Gokulchand Chali Chamanpura village in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Son of Shri Munimsinh, he completed his early education in Dabhoi, Vadodara district, and briefly pursued engineering at Nirma University, Ahmedabad before choosing to follow his childhood dream of serving in the Indian Army. He joined the Army in 2003 and was inducted into the Corps of Signals, a vital arm responsible for military communications. Over the next 14 years, he served in various operational areas across the country. A seasoned soldier, he was also part of the elite NSG team that conducted the counter-terrorist operation during the 26/11 Mumbai attacks. While clearing the Taj Hotel of terrorists, he displayed exceptional bravery by carrying an injured Subedar Major to safety amidst heavy enemy fire. For this act of gallantry, he was awarded the Vishisht Seva Medal. Later, Lance Naik Bhandoriya Gopalsinh Munimsinh was deputed to 1 Rashtriya Rifles, tasked with counter-insurgency operations in Jammu & Kashmir. On 12 February 2017, based on credible intelligence about militants hiding in a house in Frisal village, Kulgam district, a joint operation was launched by 1 Rashtriya Rifles, Jammu and Kashmir Police, and the 18th Battalion of the CRPF. As the security forces closed in, the militants opened fire, sparking a fierce gun battle that lasted over 10 hours. In the final phase of the operation, Lance Naik Bhandoriya Gopalsinh Munimsinh and Lance Naik Raghubeer Singh formed the leading assault pair to storm the house. In an extraordinary act of courage, they attacked the entrenched militants but were gravely injured in the firefight and later succumbed to their injuries. For his conspicuous bravery, selfless devotion to duty, and supreme sacrifice in the face of the enemy, Lance Naik Bhandoriya Gopalsinh Munimsinh was posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra.

Name: Harmandeep Singh Baidwan
Biography: Shaurya Chakra/ 04 December 2004 Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan, Service Number IC-54305, served with honour in the Indian Army as an officer of the 6 Rajputana Rifles. Born to Mr. K. S. Baidwan and Smt. G. K. Baidwan, he hailed from Ropar and was known for his commitment, courage, and exemplary sense of duty. Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan launched a cordon and search operation in a village in District Anantnag, Jammu & Kashmir. At 1605 hours on 04 December 2004 when search was in progress, suspicious movement was observed near a mosque. Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan immediately sealed off the area. The parties came under intense and effective fire from terrorists hiding inside the mosque. He laid concertina coils and lighting system around the mosque. Realising grave danger to own troops, Major Baidwan crawled through adjoining Nala along with small team and reached outside mosque without detection. In a flash, smoke grenade was thrown inside and rush drill executed with speed. Major Baidwan, displaying exceptional courage at his own peril, engaged a terrorist close to the window in fierce combat, killing him instantly. The other two terrorists lobbed grenades at him. Undeterred and realising danger to his buddies, he repeatedly exposed himself to danger simultaneously releasing grenades towards the terrorists. In a flash, displaying conspicuous bravery, he charged at one terrorist and sprayed a burst killing him at point blank range. The third terrorist made a desperate charge firing at him. Major Baidwan grappled with the terrorist in a dare devil hand to hand duel, snatched his weapon and shot him in a super human effort. Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan displayed raw courage, initiative and inspiring leadership in fighting the terrorists.

Name: MAYAN GOPAL
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous) / 18 June 1994 https://gallantryawards.gov.in/awardee/2178 Subedar Mayan Gopal was enrolled in the MADRAS Regiment. The JCO led a column in the cordon and search operation in Pulwama dist on 18 June 1994. On observing suspicious movements of militants along a nallah early morning, Subedar Mayan moved to an adjacent high ground to intercept them. However, the party led by Subedar Mayan and some militants who approached from a different direction reached the high ground simultaneously. The Subedar with nerves of steel and cool courage personally led the charge on militants against stiff and heavy automatic fire and killed a militant. Subedar Mayan was himself seriously injured too. Unmindful of his own injury and personal safety, the JCO continued to chase yet another militant. At close range, the militant stood up face with Subedar Mayan and both fired simultaneously. Though the militant was shot dead, Subedar Mayan was again hit and died instantly. During this fierce encounter Subedar Mayan had displayed exceptional leadership and unparalleled courage, for this act of outstanding valour devotion to duty, Subedar Mayan Gopal was awarded Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous).

Name: KARN VEER SINGH
Citation Details: 20th October 2021 Based on specific HUMINT regarding movement of two unidentified terrorists in a village in Shopian district (Jammu and Kashmir) an ambush was laid on 20 October 2021. Sepoy Karn Veer Singh was scout of the team which had laid the ambush. At 1030 hours, when intercepted by the ambush, both the terrorists in an attempt to escape jumped into a nalla. Sepoy Karn Veer Singh foreseeing the contingency of terrorists escape dashed after them alone for 100 meters. Terrorists realizing that they were being chased fired at him indiscriminately and lobbed grenades injuring him. Undaunted by his injuries, Sepoy Karn Veer Singh crawled ahead for 30 meters and accurately engaged the terrorists and pinned them down. Valorous at close range, he eliminated terrorist in an intense firefight. Displaying unprecedented courage and devotion to duty Sepoy Karn Veer Singh continued to engage the second terrorist, injured him before receiving a bullet injury on his head, and laid his life in the line of duty. For eliminating one hardcore terrorist and injuring another one, despite being mortally wounded, Sepoy Karn Veer Singh is awarded of SHAURYA CHAKRA (POSTHUMOUS)

Name: AMAR NATH MISHRA
Biography: Constable Amarnath Mishra of the CRPF played a crucial role in the success of a major antiMaoist operation conducted in the Aurangabad-Gaya region on 07 January 2016. The operation originated from intelligence inputs suggesting the presence of a Maoist group in the dense forests of Bhaluahi, Gopaldera, Morma, Kachnar, Chhuchiya, and Dulare, under the jurisdiction of Dhibra and Dumariya police stations. Commandant Rabish Kumar Singh of 205 CoBRA planned the mission with emphasis on secrecy, deploying only two compact, highly trained teams: one under Assistant Commandant Chandan Kumar and the other under Assistant Commandant Gufran Ahmad, supported by a small local police element. Both teams moved from Bhaluahi camp under the cover of darkness, carefully avoiding Maoist surveillance networks. After a full day of combing without contact, they halted at a vantage point, where their vigilance paid off. Around 1715 hrs, smoke rising from a nearby hillock suggested Maoist activity. Recognising the opportunity, Assistant Commandant Chandan Kumar silently coordinated a three-directional approach, with Constable Mishra advancing in the south-west element. As the troops ascended toward the suspected site in fading light, the Maoists detected movement and unleashed heavy fire. Despite the sudden threat and the wounding of Head Constable Nagendra Prasad, the assault continued. During the charge, Constable Mishra and his commander confronted a sentry position at close range. The Maoists attempted to escape while firing indiscriminately, but in a bold and rapid counter-move, both troopers closed the distance and neutralised them. Maoist fire intensified, including grenade attacks, yet Constable Mishra remained composed, advancing further under extremely limited cover. When two Maoists attempted to break out toward their position while firing, Mishra and his commander reacted instantly. They moved laterally, engaged the fleeing militants at close quarters, and inflicted injuries that forced them back into the jungle. The firefight continued until darkness set in. A search at first light revealed four Maoists killed, including senior regional and zonal commanders, along with significant weapons and equipment. Constable Amarnath Mishra’s conduct during the operation reflected exceptional courage, steadfastness, and an unflinching commitment to duty in a highly volatile combat environment.

Name: SANDEEP KUMAR
Citation Details: 05 January 2022 Since March 2020, Major Sandeep Kumar exhibited exceptional resoluteness and fortitude during five successful operations resulting in elimination of 13 terrorists. On 05 January 2022 at 0430 hours, during a specific operation in, Pulwama district (Jammu and Kashmir), three terrorists equipped with modern assault rifles and night vision devices opened indiscriminate fire on search party on Major Sandeep from a cowshed. Maintaining tactical composure, he swiftly retaliated fire and re-deployed his team to prevent terrorist escape. Undeterred by terrorist fire and with utter disregard to personal safety, the officer crawled ahead under covering fire provided by his buddy and closed in to the cowshed in an open area without any cover. The terrorists opened indiscriminate fire on Major Sandeep and his buddy. Displaying unflinching loyalty, he pushed his buddy away from grave danger, exposing himself to heavy terrorist fire. In an act of unparalleled courage, he engaged terrorists in a face to face gun fight eliminating one terrorist and grievously injuring another terrorist. Terrorist eliminated was identified as a Category ‘A++’ terrorist. For displaying supreme leadership and exemplary courage beyond the call of duty, Major Sandeep Kumar awarded of SHAURYA CHAKRA

Name: AZIZ MOHD
Biography: Lance Havildar Aziz Mohd of the 20 Jammu and Kashmir Rifles served with exemplary dedication and courage in the Indian Army. On 11 May 2008, acting on information that terrorists had taken civilians hostage at Kali Mandi, Samba (Jammu & Kashmir), the unit launched an operation to rescue the captives and neutralise the threat. Lance Havildar Aziz Mohd was part of the column deployed for the task and played a leading role in the close-cordon operation. Under intense terrorist fire, he led the rescue effort with remarkable composure and bravery, successfully evacuating five women, three children, and one man to safety. During the operation, when the terrorists attempted to escape, he confronted them directly, killing one on the spot despite being seriously wounded in the exchange. As the second terrorist charged at him, he again stood his ground and, disregarding his own safety and the pain of his injuries, shot the terrorist dead before succumbing to his wounds. Through his steadfast courage, presence of mind, and supreme devotion to duty, Lance Havildar Aziz Mohd saved several innocent lives and eliminated both terrorists in close combat. He made the supreme sacrifice in the finest traditions of the Indian Army. For his exceptional bravery and selfless service, he was awarded the Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous) on 26 January 2009.

Name: MEHAR SINGH DAHIYA
Biography: Colonel (Then Major) Mehar Singh Dahiya was born at village Sehri (now in Sonipat district) then in Rohtak district. He is a third generation Soldier. His grandfather and father Defadar Ch. Maha Singh had together served in 17 Poona Horse and participated in some of the fiercest battles fought in Mesopotamia (present day Iraq) in World War II. Defadar Ch. Maha Singh was a battle causality with lifelong 100 percent disability pension. 1 Since childhood, Mehar Singh knew he was destined to be a soldier. He had initial education at the village school and did secondary from Sainik School, Chittorgarh, and later went on to join 42 Course at the prestigious National Defence Academy, Khadakwasla, Pune in 21 July,1969. He was part of India Squadron and passed out with his course in June 1972. Later on he joined Indian Military Academy and passed out n 17 June 1973. He was commissioned into Jammu and Kashmir Militia (later 3 Jammu & Kashmir Light Infantry) (JAK LI) in June 1973.2 He is married to Smt Pushpa, and the couple have a son, who is a fourth generation army officer. He commanded 3 JAK LI, becoming the first CO of his unit who was directly commissioned from IMA and commanded his unit from 1992 to 1995. He held many staff and instructional appointments at category A and B Army establishments, including as a GTO at SSB Bangalore and later, Allahabad. During his posting to Ladakh Scouts where he became Major and Company Commander 1 The GAP team is deeply grateful to Colonel M S Dahiya, Shaurya Chakra for providing us with information, details and photographs. 2 Dabas, Dilbag. “The Tribune.” The Tribune, 2019, www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/haryanatribune/mehar-dahiya-hero-of-battle-for-vital-saddle-in-siachen-716149/. Accessed 28 July 2025. As Group Testing Officer at Selection Centre, Bangalore, he spotted and cleared Major Rajiv Kumar Joon, AC, SC and Second Lieutenant Rakesh Singh, AC. The two gallantry awardees who were commissioned into 22 Grenadiers and were awarded Ashoka Chakra posthumously for bravery during counter-insurgency operations. The Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry (JAK LI) is an infantry regiment of the Indian Army with a distinctive and multifaceted regimental history. In 1947, following the incursion of Pakistani troops into Indian territory, local militias were formed from residents of Jammu, Nubra, Leh, and Srinagar. These units were subsequently restructured from home guards into a formal militia. Initially designated as the Jammu and Kashmir Militia, a total of eight battalions were placed under the administrative control of the Indian Ministry of Home Affairs and received corresponding funding. Due to their exemplary performance in military operations during 1962, 1965, and 1971, these battalions were formally inducted as a regular infantry regiment of the Indian Army in 1974. The JAK LI holds several unique distinctions within the Indian Army. It is the only regiment raised post-Independence, unlike other regiments that trace their lineage to the British Indian Army. Additionally, it is the sole regiment composed entirely of civilian volunteers who mobilized in response to the invasion by Pakistani tribal forces (Kabailis). Another notable feature is its highly integrated structure, with personnel from diverse religious backgrounds serving together at all levels, down to the smallest detachment units. Today, the JAK LI is recognized as one of the most decorated regiments in the Indian Army, having received honors ranging from the Param Vir Chakra to Mentions in Despatches. The militia demonstrated exceptional valor during the 1965 Indo-Pak War. However, it was their gallant actions in the 1971 conflict that earned them three battle honours. Beyond conventional warfare, the JAK LI has participated in international operations, including deployment with the Indian Peacekeeping Force in Sri Lanka (1987) and the United Nations Mission in Somalia. In 1984, the regiment was also deployed to the Siachen Glacier as part of Operation MEGHDOOT, further cementing its operational legacy. OPERATION MEGHDOOT Operation MEGHDOOT is an ongoing operation along North-Western Border region of India in high altitude area of Siachen Glacier, ranging above 21000 feet. Launched on 13 April 1984, this unique military operation was the first assault launched in the world's highest battlefield. The military action resulted in Indian troops gaining control of the strategically located Siachen Glacier. It is considered as a feat unparalleled in the history of high-altitude warfare where soldiers of Indian Army and Air Force operate under most adverse weather conditions with sub-zero temperatures of minus 50°C. The Siachen Glacier is the second longest glacier in the world. The scroll of honour at Indian Army’s Siachen Base Camp reads, “Quartered in snow, silent to remain. When the bugle calls, they shall rise and march again.” Beneath the veneer of this bleak beauty lie menacing hazards that snatch away human lives if one is not careful. Given the significance of this Glacier, it provided a strategic importance to India, Pakistan and China as it served as a hub for Shaksham Valley and Karakoram Pass.4 On 13 Apr 1984, ‘Operation Meghdoot’ was launched in the world’s highest battlefield with an aim to wrest control of the strategic heights on the Saltoro Ridge, overlooking the Nubra Valley. 3 Siachen area has been a bone of contention between Pakistan and India for many years. The root cause of the issue can be traced back to the Karachi Agreement of 1949. The representatives of both the nations drew the ‘Ceasefire Line’ across maps of Jammu and Kashmir from Manawar in the South, to Khor in the North and thence ‘North to the Glaciers’ through NJ 9842. Presumably when the discussion came up on the glaciated wilderness of snow and ice the representatives stopped at grid Point NJ 9842 on the presumption that neither side would be interested in contesting an area where not a blade of grass grows and even breathing is a problem. The problem started when Pakistan decided to further their ambitions which complicated the issue. They illegally ceded some 5180 square kilometers of Indian territory to China in the area where the boundaries of India, Pakistan and China meet thereby altering the geo-strategic importance of this area. Secondly, by permitting and assisting foreign mountaineering and scientific expeditions in the area it raised the issue of ‘rights’ in an area that did not belong to them. The cartographic ambiguities of 1962 and Pakistan’s growing devious nature had concerned the Indian Army. In mid-seventies reports of foreign mountaineering expeditions crossing the Saltoro Ridge and Siachen Glacier from Pakistan side came to India’s notice. It was also learnt that Pakistan Army officers accompanied these expeditions. As a result of these reports to establish our own claim to the area a mountaineering expedition led by one of the Indian Army’s leading mountaineers, Colonel Narinder (Bull) Kumar, was sent to area in 1978. The expedition went to Tersam Kangri and in 1984 the Indian Army took pre-emptive action and occupied Saltoro Range. 4 In early 1985, the Pakistan military was under increasing pressure to give a befitting reply to India’s occupation. Therefore, the buildup of troops on the Pakistani side steadily increased. A Northern Command intelligence assessment at that time estimated that Task Force HQ, carved out of 62 Infantry Brigade was established at Khapalu. Elements from the Gilgit-based 323 Infantry Brigade were also pushed ahead for glacier operations. The note said: “The following units were officially part of the Siachen deployment from the Pakistani side by NovemberDecember1984: 21 POK Battalion, 1 Northern Light Infantry (NLI) Battalion supported by one company of 9 NLI and one company (Shaheen) of 1 SSG Battalion. An independent mountain battery from the 452 (I) artillery regiment equipped with 105 mm guns, one battery of 88 (independent) mountain battery equipped with 120 mm mortars and an ad hoc commando company raised under the 80 Infantry Brigade.” 3 Kulkarni, Ramesh, and Anjali Karpe. Siachen 1987: Battle for the frozen frontier. Gurugram, Haryana: HarperCollins Publishers India, 2022. 4 Gokhale, Nitin A. Beyond NJ 9842: The Siachen Saga. Bloomsbury India Publishing, 2014. Major Mehar Singh Dahiya’s Leadership in the Siachen Conflict (1984–1985) In October 1984, Major Mehar Singh Dahiya was posted to Headquarters Ladakh Scouts and assumed command of E Company, stationed at Phukche, with a platoon deployed at Demchok—the point where the Indus River enters Indian territory from Tibet/China. In December 1984, at short notice, he was reassigned to the Karakoram Range and given command of Delta Company in the Siachen Glacier. His company’s area of responsibility extended from Kumar DZ to Sia La Pass. The Indian Army had secured the Siachen Glacier in April 1984, preempting Pakistani forces without direct combat. However, while the initial occupation was achieved swiftly, the subsequent establishment of five permanent posts under extreme conditions presented an entirely different challenge. This feat was accomplished under the exceptional leadership of Major Niranjan Singh Salaria, supported by five officers, a dozen Junior Commissioned Officers (JCOs), and over two hundred troops. From May 1984 to February 1985, the sector remained relatively quiet. It is a recorded history today that Pakistan Army was left red faced but, literally opted to do something impossible in that terrain and climatic condition in the month of December-January. Upon assuming command, Major Dahiya conducted a thorough operational and logistical assessment of the situation. He realised that something was amiss, and prepared himself with meagre resources of men and material. The Operation (19 February 1985) On 19 February 1985, after a seven-day wait, a helicopter arrived on a routine resupply mission. Suspecting enemy activity—screened from his position by Point 5966—Major Dahiya instructed the pilot to conduct an aerial reconnaissance over the Kondus Glacier. Within minutes, the pilot confirmed the presence of Pakistani forces. Major Dahiya immediately dispatched the pilot to alert Brigadier Jal Master, the 26 Sector Commander. Moments later, the enemy, realizing their cover had been compromised, opened heavy machine gun (HMG) fire from Point 5966 onto Sia La Pass, leaving the company headquarters vulnerable. With only 23 men available, Major Dahiya assembled a team of 15, leaving Captain Dr. M.L. Bhat to defend Sia La Pass against a potential assault from the Kundus Glacier—a tactically plausible scenario. Had the enemy exploited this opportunity, they could have jeopardized Major Dahiya’s advance toward the strategically critical saddle at Point 5966, where Pakistani forces had already positioned their HMG. At 1820 hours, without artillery support, Major Dahiya led his men on an arduous 11-hour climb through crevassed terrain, navigating slopes of 72–75 degrees in 5–7 feet of soft snow. They successfully secured the saddle, just 200 meters from the enemy’s HMG position. For the next six days, at an altitude of approximately 19,000 feet and temperatures of -60°C, with no reinforcements or resupply, his unit withstood relentless mortar fire and repelled multiple assaults. Upholding the written orders of Lieutenant General P.N. Hoon, Corps Commander— to fight "to the last man, last round"—Major Dahiya’s actions decisively neutralized Pakistan’s offensive, solidifying India’s control over the Sia La sector. Major M S Dahiya being awarded Shaurya Chakra by the Hon’ble President of India Giani Zail Singh All 15 soldiers suffered severe frostbite and were evacuated to first to General Hospital, Leh and then to Command Hospital Chandigarh, where nine out of fifteen soldiers lost their limb. For their valour, the unit received five gallantry awards: one Ashoka Chakra, one Kirti Chakra, one Shaurya Chakra (awarded to Major Dahiya), and two Sena Medals. Had it not been for Major Dahiya’s swift and courageous leadership, the loss of the saddle—a dominant feature on the northern glacier—would have compromised India’s entire defensive position in the region. Post-Military Career Promoted to Lieutenant Colonel in 1989 and Colonel in 1992, he retired on 31 January 2007. Post-retirement, he served as a co-opted member of the Animal Welfare Board of India and contributed to the Haryana Academy of History and Culture. Additionally, he was a member of the Academic Planning Board at Chaudhry Ranbir Singh University (CRSU), Jind, and directed a pilot project on human transformation at CRSU. Currently, he resides in Dwarka, New Delhi. Colonel M S Dahiya pointing his name on the board of gallantry awardees in the IMA
