(Effective date of the award : 21st February, 1985) Major Mehar Singh Dahiya with a small patrol marched throughout the night over most difficult terrain at high altitude with the temperature touching minus 32 degree Celsius, high velocity winds blowing to accomplish a difficult assignment by personal example, he successfully completed his mission by personal example, he successfully completed his mission in one of the forward areas in Jammu and Kashmir. Major Mehar Singh Dahiya thus exhibited exemplary courage, resolute determination, inspiring leadership and devotion to duty of a high order. Gazette of India, Notification No.– dated

Name: MANESH PV
Biography: On 27 Nov 08, Nk PV Manesh was part of the team, tasked to locate and eliminate terrorists from Hotel Oberoi, Mumbai, where they had already killed approx. 34 civilians by then. Nk Manesh, voluntarily led his team setting personal example, rescuing 39 Foreign and Indian Nationals. The rescue operations were conducted in total darkness at night. While carrying out intervention in the suspected room, his team drew fierce fire from the terrorists. Undeterred and with utter disregard to personal safety he continued to fire on the terrorists and pinned them down foiling their efforts to escape. Immediately, he led and positioned his squad to plug the escape routes and started closing in with the door under cover fire. The terrorists opened fire and lobbed grenades at the squad, in which Nk Manesh got splinter injury in his skull and started bleeding profusely. He refused to be evacuated, kept engaging the terrorists and stormed inside the target room. During the fierce fire fight Nk PV Manesh killed one of the terrorists at close range, before losing consciousness due to loss of blood. He was evacuated to the hospital and subsequently recovered. For his undaunted valour, resolute determination and dedication towards the mission beyond the call of duty, Nk PV Manesh was awarded ‘Shaurya Chakra’.

Name: RAKESH SHARMA
Biography: Vijay Star/ July 1999 Major Rakesh Sharma was born on 04th January 1972 in a humble family in Duhuak, a small village in Bilaspur district, Himachal Pradesh in the family of Shri B R Sharma and Smt Nirmla Sharma. He received his early education at Government Senior Secondary School, Berthin (Himachal Pradesh), and BSF Senior Secondary School, Tekanpur (Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh). He later graduated from Deshbandhu College, Delhi University, before joining the Officers Training Academy. He was commissioned into the 114 Medium Regiment, Indian Army on 24 August 1996. He was posted as a young Indian Army officer in the Army's Artillery Regiment (155 MM Bofors) in Kashmir. He remained in service till 2004 . At the time of leaving, he held the rank of Major. During this period, he actively and voluntarily participated in multiple operations and consistently demonstrated exemplary courage, leadership, and professional excellence. 1 In the chilling winters on 22nd December 1998, then a young Captain, Rakesh Sharma planned and led his first major counter-terrorist operation in the Kashmir Valley. Acting on intelligence inputs regarding the presence of three terrorists plotting to target a respected local and his family, he launched a search-and-destroy mission with a team of 15 soldiers in a lowland area surrounded by hills, with scattered villages amidst dense forests. After deployment in midnight, In the early morning, the team commenced house-to-house searches. Despite exhaustive efforts until mid-afternoon, they were unable to find the terrorists. At 1500 hours, while preparing to conclude the operation, a diversionary burst of fire by the team helped in revealing presence of three armed terrorists attempting to escape. Major Sharma immediately led the chase across difficult terrain. After nearly half an hour of pursuit through dense forests, the terrorists were lost. However, subsequent interrogation of fleeing villagers exposed their hideout in a fortified stone house. Major (then Captain) Rakesh Sharma, with his troops following a successful counterterrorist operation in the Kashmir Valley, 1998 1 StartupnRise. (2021, May 18). Major Rakesh Sharma, Shaurya Chakra (Retd): Tackling the pandemic in rural hills. StartupnRise. https://startupnrise.com/major-rakesh-sharma-shaurya-chakra-retd-tackling-thepandemic-in-rural-hills/ At 1630 hours, Major Rakesh’s team surrounded the house and came under intense enemy fire. Displaying tactical acumen, he broke the door and initiated close-quarter battle. In the fierce exchange that followed, two terrorists were neutralized inside the house. With darkness setting in, the possibility of a third terrorist posed a constant threat. The situation escalated when the hidden militant opened fire from a wooden grain box inside the house, forcing the team to disengage temporarily. Maintaining composure, Captain Rakesh Sharma reorganized his troops and re-established control of the operation. Throughout the night, the team held its positions. It successfully prevented any breakout. Further intelligence confirmed that the remaining terrorist was the injured commander of the outfit. At first light, Major Rakesh Sharma launched the final assault. A well-coordinated fire from multiple directions suppressed resistance from the militants, enabling the his troops to storm the house. The team led by Captain Rakesh used precision fire, and neutralised the third terrorist. The operation lasted for more than 30 hours, and resulted in the killing of three terrorists without any casualties on the Indian forces. In an interview with Deccan Chronicle, Major Rakesh Sharma recalls the opening days of Indian operations during the 1999 Kargil War, describing how, “in the very first week,” he and his battery were stationed roughly 600 km away, on the opposite side of the Pir Panjal Range. The moment orders arrived, they were preparing lunch: ammunition was being stored underground; villagers came and helped to load the heavy rounds. Despite minimal preparation time, the battery made contact with the area, loaded up, and moved out the same day. After three nights of movement, they crossed Zojila just past midnight; by 4:00 a.m., team led by Capt Rakesh with is 155 MM Bofors guns were already “pounding enemy locations. 2 The first major ridgeline to fall was Tololing in the Drass sub-sector on May 29, 1999. The Tololing ridgeline was the closest to the Srinagar–Leh NH 1A, and its early clearance was an operational priority. Point 4590, a high mountain top on this ridge, was captured on June 13, 1999. Point 5140, the highest feature on the Tololing Ridge, was captured after several weeks of bitter fighting on June 20, 1999, after a simultaneous, multi-directional attack was launched by assaulting columns from three different infantry battalions. All the attacks were preceded by sustained fire assaults from over one hundred artillery guns, mortars, and rocket launchers. Thousands of shells, bombs, and rocket warheads wreaked havoc on the objectives and prevented the enemy from interfering with the assault till the fire was lifted for reasons of safety. The 105 mm IFG and 155 mm Bofors medium guns, firing in the direct firing role, destroyed all visible enemy sangars and forced the enemy to abandon his positions. The arcs of fire trailing behind the Bofors high explosive shells and the Grad rockets provided an awesome sight and instilled the fear of Allah into the minds of Pakistan's soldiers. 3 Over a hundred guns delivered murderous fire assaults. Over 1,200 rounds of high explosive rained down on Tiger Hill in the space of five minutes and caused large-scale death and devastation. The Gunners of the Indian artillery fired their guns audaciously in the direct firing role under the very noses of Pakistani artillery OPs, completely disregarding personal safety. 2 Deccan Chronicle. 2018. "You Can Take Soldier Out of Army, but..." Deccan Chronicle, July 26, 2018. https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/in-other-news/260718/you-can-take-soldier-out-of-army-but.html 3 Kanwal, Gurmeet. Heroes of Kargil. New Delhi: Ritana Books, 2002. In another uniquely effective innovation, even 122 mm Grad MBRLs were employed in the direct firing role. Hundreds of shells and rocket warheads impacted on the pinnacle of Tiger Hill in full view of the TV cameras, and the nation watched in rapt attention as the might of the Regiment of Artillery burst forth in magnificent glory. In recognition of the significant contribution made by the artillery regiments that participated in this battle, Point 4875 was renamed "Gun Hill"—an immense honour bestowed on the artillery. Due to the massive employment of all available firepower resources to decimate the enemy's defences, 18 Grenadiers, the heroes of Tiger Hill, did not suffer a single casualty during the final assault. By honouring three artillery regiments with the Unit Citation for battles in Kargil (141 Field Regiment, 197 Field Regiment, and 108 Medium Regiment), Army Headquarters acknowledged the immense part played by all the units of the Regiment of Artillery in the gallant fight to recapture Indian territory from the Pakistani intruders. 4 It was in this setting that the Bofors howitzer demonstrated its value. Despite the controversy over its induction into service, the 155 mm FH 77-B Bofors medium howitzer performed remarkably well and was the mainstay of artillery firepower in Kargil. Its maximum range of 30 km enabled deep strikes at the enemy's gun positions, administrative installations, ammunition dumps, and headquarters, besides destroying forward positions held by the intruders. By moving up these guns into advanced gun positions for direct fire on Tololing and Tiger Hill, literally under the nose of the enemy and thereby inviting certain enemy artillery fire onto themselves, the Gunners exhibited unparalleled courage in battle. Among the officers who played a pivotal role was Major Rakesh Sharma of the Bofors Regiment. During the intense fighting in the Tololing subsector, he displayed exemplary courage and leadership in manning forward gun positions under heavy enemy retaliation. His battery carried out a sustained bombardment for 48–72 hours during peak phases, and he was coordinating closely with Forward Observers (FOs) to execute corrected fire accurately. His accurate fire direction and coordination ensured that the infantry assaulting columns of 2 RAJPUTANA RIFLES received timely and devastating artillery support. At critical stages of the battle, when Pakistani positions were holding up Indian advances, Major Rakesh Sharma personally supervised the adjustment of fire plans, bringing down accurate salvos on wellcamouflaged enemy sangars. His steadfastness under fire not only inspired his gun crews but also directly contributed to breaking the enemy’s stronghold on the dominating heights. 5 The coordination between the artillery regiments and the assaulting battalions, notably 2 RAJPUTANA RIFLES, proved decisive. Each infantry push was preceded by carefully timed bombardments that pinned enemy troops and neutralised observation posts and at times the infantry created clear corridors to bring down accurate direct fire of Bofors on the objective. Over several days of combined action, this combined effort wore down the enemy resistance. By 13 June 1999, Tololing was retaken, marking the first major Indian success in this war. After a highly successful and productive tenure at Kargil in 1999 Capt Rakesh briefly volunteered to participate in Operation Parakram in which He and 2 team members were 4 Ibid Sharma, Rakesh. 2025. Indian Army Operational Stories | Maj Rakesh Sharma SC | A Shaurya Chakra Story. DEF Talks by Aadi. July 4, 2025. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K0IAAWckpD8 5 specially trained to operate as Commando OP officers beyond enemy lines in desert warfare . This training was highly demanding and grueling with days spend in isolation and hiding undetected in deserts under the sand. Post Operation Parakram deployment Major Rakesh again volunteered to go back to Operational areas of Kashmir Valley and was transferred to 18 Rastriya Rifles as Company Commander in September 2002 in the most dreaded valley of Lolab Operation in Kashmir 2003 After setting up a new company base Maj Rakesh planned and led many successful Counter terror operations . It was the operation in 2003, which earned him the prestigious Shaurya Chakra award. During the peak of insurgency in the Kashmir valley in early 2003, Major Rakesh Sharma was commanding a company at Somvir Post. Acting on specific intelligence inputs, Major Rakesh Sharma led an operation into Village Doruswain on 25 June 2003. Displaying ingenuity and maintaining complete surprise, he stealthily placed stops and effectively sealed the area. While leading his party to cordon the house, his team suddenly came face to face with terrorists emerging from the house. Keeping his composure, he acted swiftly and shot dead two terrorists. A fierce firefight followed in total darkness. With complete disregard for his own safety, Major Rakesh crawled forward to close in on the terrorists. Two of them charged out, firing indiscriminately. Unnerved and reflexive, from a flank position, he engaged them at pointblank range, killing both. In the pitch-dark encounter that followed, he seized the initiative, closed in on the terrorists with a very high degree of field craft, and neutralized two more at close range. Total of five terrorists were neutralized in this operation, of which Major Rakesh Sharma personally killed three Pakistani and one Afghani militant. For exceptional gallantry, skill in planning, execution of the highest order, and exemplary leadership under trying circumstances, Major Rakesh Sharma was awarded the Shaurya Chakra. Major Rakesh Sharma receiving the Shaurya Chakra from the Hon’ble President of India, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, during the Defence Investiture Ceremony in 2004 Major Rakesh Sharma actively participated in, Operation Rakshak, Operation Parakram and several counter-insurgency operations in Kashmir, demonstrating leadership and operational skill throughout his service. He superannuated in July 2004 while serving as Company Commander, 18 Rashtriya Rifles. Corporate Tenure After a highly active, productive and successful Army tenure Major Rakesh Sharma took up a management executive program at prestigious IIMB and worked in corporate in many leadership positions in Telecom, Construction as well as Banking Industry till December 2023. Major Rakesh was also instrumental in setting up first Defence Banking team in a leading corporate Bank. As part of giving back to society Major Rakesh has established a school for not so privileged children in the suburbs of Delhi. The institution is named Shaurya School. The school presently educates and nurtures around 125 children per year, providing them with opportunities for growth and learning. Major Rakesh Sharma is now is a social entrepreneur and owns a Echo tourist Resort in the hills of Uttarakhand where as he has mainly employed youth of rural belt creating Job Opportunities for them. Further he has launched another Startup in the field of publishing Industry mainly to ease out the issues faced by authors and writers, especially with an objective to find out suitable publishers for their writings. Major Rakesh is part of many Ex Servicemen leagues especially those in rural area’s and is involved in helping veterans and Veer Naari’s to resolve their various issues with local administration. Beyond being a motivational speaker Major Rakesh Sharma is a prominent guest speaker and panelist at various Organizations to include Corporates, Universities and various other educational institutions.

Name: SURENDRAN NAIR K
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous) / 2 August 1992 https://gallantryawards.gov.in/awardee/2006 LNk Surendran Nair K, SC (P) On the 2 August 1992, at 2.00 in the after-noon, bn with a platoon of another Bn, moved to cordon an area near Usman village in Taran Taran district of Punjab, where the police was engaged in an encounter with the terrorists who were concealed in a ditch screened by thick sarkanda grass. Lance Naik K Surendran Nair spotted another cemented drain, also covered with Sarkanda. He moved stealthily towards this, when he was barely 5 meters away from his objective, a terrorist opened fire, and lance Naik Surendran Nair was wounded in his abdomen, Despite being mortally wounded, he charged with his LMG firing from the hip and grievously injured his assailant, although he received another burst of bullets, this time on the chest, he continued to bring down accurate fire on the terrorist, till at last he fell unconscious with his finger still on the trigger, he was evacuated to military Hospital, Amritsar where he succumbed to his injuries. The man he had mortally wounded was Ram Rajinder Singh, a Category ‘A’ list of Bhinderwala Tiger force of Kalistan (Sangha group), who carried a cash award of rupees one lakh on his head. Lance Naik K. Surendran Nair, displayed courage, outstanding devotion to duty, and rare spirit of self-sacrifice in his fight against the terrorist.

Name: MALUK CHAND
Biography: Lance Naik Maluk Chand of 16 Dogra Regiment was part of a search and destroy mission launched with a small team in the Swan area of Jammu and Kashmir on 10 May 1999. During the operation, the column came under intense fire from well-entrenched militants, leaving all ranks exposed in open ground under heavy fire. With exceptional alertness and courage, he immediately brought his Light Machine Gun into action, preventing a potential disaster. Despite being in full view of the militants and under continuous fire, he held his ground and kept engaging the enemy with accurate bursts. When a bullet struck him in the throat, he refused to withdraw, continuing to fire until his comrades were able to reposition. Grievously wounded and bleeding, he then charged towards the militants, killing one in close combat and, even in his dying moments, indicated the direction of escape of the last militant. For his conspicuous gallantry, devotion to duty, and supreme sacrifice, Lance Naik Maluk Chand was awarded the Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous).

Name: ANUJ SOOD
Biography: Major Anuj Sood, served as a Company Commander with 21 Rashtriya Rifles in Kupwara district, Jammu & Kashmir, and was engaged in counter-insurgency operations. Between 29 April and 03 May 2020, he was involved in a critical sequence of actions that ultimately demonstrated his unwavering courage and commitment to protecting civilian lives. On 01 May 2020, after receiving precise intelligence about the presence of two terrorists in the Watsar Forest, Major Sood quickly initiated an operation to intercept them. When the terrorists were sighted, they responded with indiscriminate gunfire before attempting to escape. Major Sood and his team returned controlled fire, preventing civilian casualties despite the hostile situation. The following day, 02 May 2020, the terrorists were traced again to a location in Chanjimula. Recognising the threat posed to civilians being held hostage, Major Sood personally joined the assault team consisting of the Commanding Officer and three other soldiers. With complete disregard for his own safety, he advanced into the target house under heavy fire. His resolute actions helped secure the release of three civilians. In an effort to rescue the remaining two hostages, he physically engaged one of the terrorists inside the structure. During this intense encounter, he sustained multiple gunshot wounds while ensuring the safety of the civilians. For his remarkable bravery, supreme sacrifice, and steadfast dedication to duty, Major Anuj Sood was posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra.

Name: SANJAY KAUSHIK
Biography: Shaurya Chakra / 01 July 2009 On 01 July 2009 at 1300h, IC-46936F Lieutenant Colonel Sanjay Kaushik leading the Battalion Ghatak column, moved on reliable input about presence of four terrorists in house of a suspect at village Nilsu. On spot interrogation, provided input that the terrorists were likely to be hiding in the adjoining forest. The officer displayed tactical acumen by immediately resisting the cordon and coordinating a two pronged probe to locate terrorists in the forest which had dense foliage and steep slopes. On being probed, the terrorists fired on own parties spread along a nala, covered with big boulders and dense foliage. The fire fight continued in heavy rainstorm for approx two hours, when the officer anticipating approaching fading light, crawled forward from a flank against heavy fire and charged after throwing grenades. Disregarding personal safety, he closed in and killed two terrorists from point blank range and facilitated neutralization of the third terrorist. For this act of gallantry, he was awarded Shaurya Chakra on 26 Jan 2010.

Name: MANISH PANDEY
Biography: Shaurya Chakra/ 11 July 2005 Lieutenant Manish Pandey Lieutenant Manish Pandey served with honour in the Indian Army as an officer of the 20 Punjab Regiment. Born to Mr. Narendra Pandey and Mrs. Pushpa Pandey, he hailed from Keonjhar and was known for his dedication, discipline, and leadership qualities. A committed officer, he exemplified courage and professionalism in carrying out his duties, earning the respect of his peers and subordinates alike. Lieutenant Manish Pandey tracked and repeatedly engaged a terrorist group in extremely rugged high altitude terrain in Northern Sector in successive multiple contacts. On 11lth July 2005, although hopelessly outnumbered by terrorists holding dominating ground, Lieutenant Manish Pandey displayed exceptional courage and tenacity to close in and engaged the terrorists in a fierce fire-fight. Undeterred by effective fire from two directions, he charged on and personally eliminated two terrorists. He, thereafter, kept his nerve to skilfully direct and inspire his men to maintain contact throughout the day and manoeuvred his team to an advantageous position by night. on 12 July, when part of his team was pinned down by effective terrorist fire, he with indomitable courage and inspiring leadership moved to a flank and eliminated. two more terrorists in a fierce close engagement. Unmindful of administrative constraints, he maintained ©pressure on the terrorists and shot two more terrcrists. In the ensuing search of the area, bodies of 18 terrorists were recovered. Lieutenant Manish Pandey displayed raw courage, singular bravéry and leadership in the finest traditions of the Indian Army, in fighting the terrorists.

Name: VIJAY SINGH
Biography: Major Vijay Singh, son of Shri Sher Singh, from District Jammu, Jammu and Kashmir, was a commissioned officer of the Jammu and Kashmir Rifles Regiment of the Indian Army. A resolute and professionally accomplished officer, he exemplified the regiment’s enduring ethos of discipline, leadership, and battlefield composure under pressure. On 15 May 1980, his battalion was deployed to counter hostile activity in the Imphal area. The next day, 16 May 1980, Major Vijay Singh led a patrol party on a reconnaissance mission. During the operation, a jeep approaching from the opposite direction suddenly opened fire on the patrol. Reacting with exceptional presence of mind, he returned fire and shot the armed occupant in the front seat. Without hesitation, he deboarded his vehicle, rallied his men, and directed them to take positions under fire. In the exchange that followed, all three militants were killed, and their jeep with arms and ammunition was recovered. One of the slain men was later identified as a wanted criminal involved in several robbery cases. Major Vijay Singh’s courage, quick decision-making, and effective leadership ensured mission success and the safety of his troops. For his exemplary bravery and devotion to duty, he was awarded the Shaurya Chakra on 26 January 1981.

Name: Harmandeep Singh Baidwan
Biography: Shaurya Chakra/ 04 December 2004 Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan, Service Number IC-54305, served with honour in the Indian Army as an officer of the 6 Rajputana Rifles. Born to Mr. K. S. Baidwan and Smt. G. K. Baidwan, he hailed from Ropar and was known for his commitment, courage, and exemplary sense of duty. Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan launched a cordon and search operation in a village in District Anantnag, Jammu & Kashmir. At 1605 hours on 04 December 2004 when search was in progress, suspicious movement was observed near a mosque. Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan immediately sealed off the area. The parties came under intense and effective fire from terrorists hiding inside the mosque. He laid concertina coils and lighting system around the mosque. Realising grave danger to own troops, Major Baidwan crawled through adjoining Nala along with small team and reached outside mosque without detection. In a flash, smoke grenade was thrown inside and rush drill executed with speed. Major Baidwan, displaying exceptional courage at his own peril, engaged a terrorist close to the window in fierce combat, killing him instantly. The other two terrorists lobbed grenades at him. Undeterred and realising danger to his buddies, he repeatedly exposed himself to danger simultaneously releasing grenades towards the terrorists. In a flash, displaying conspicuous bravery, he charged at one terrorist and sprayed a burst killing him at point blank range. The third terrorist made a desperate charge firing at him. Major Baidwan grappled with the terrorist in a dare devil hand to hand duel, snatched his weapon and shot him in a super human effort. Major Harmandeep Singh Baidwan displayed raw courage, initiative and inspiring leadership in fighting the terrorists.

Name: KRISHNA MURTHY G
Biography: Shaurya Chakra/ 08 August 2002 LNk Krishna Murthy G was RL No 1 at FDL Tent of a MADRAS Bn. On 08 Aug 2002 ambush deployed in Manju OP Area sensed a group of terrorists attempting to infiltrate under thick cloud cover. LNk Krishna Murthy exercised restrain and allowed the terrorists to enter into preselected killing area. LNk K Murthy sprung the ambush by cleverly firing a claymore mind. The terrorists were badly wounded and started fleeing back towards Line of Control. They were engaged by AGL, MMG and 81 mm Mor fire. During search LNk Murthy relentlessly followed the blood trails to very near the Line of Control, there the party came under heavy terrorists fire. Unmindful of heavy fire by enemy FDLs and terrorists, he located the terrorists and accurately fired RL round killing two terrorists. The LNk then again closed in with the remaining terrorists, now almost on the Line of Control and in yet another swift and daring move killed another terrorist trying to move towards enemy FDL. Operation was concluded by killing the remaining terrorist. LNk Krishna Murthy G led from the front, displaying indomitable fighting spirit and cool courage. His physical and mental endurance was an epitome of conspicuous gallantry beyond the call of duty and for which he was awarded Shaurya Chakra.

Name: AMAR NATH MISHRA
Biography: Constable Amarnath Mishra of the CRPF played a crucial role in the success of a major antiMaoist operation conducted in the Aurangabad-Gaya region on 07 January 2016. The operation originated from intelligence inputs suggesting the presence of a Maoist group in the dense forests of Bhaluahi, Gopaldera, Morma, Kachnar, Chhuchiya, and Dulare, under the jurisdiction of Dhibra and Dumariya police stations. Commandant Rabish Kumar Singh of 205 CoBRA planned the mission with emphasis on secrecy, deploying only two compact, highly trained teams: one under Assistant Commandant Chandan Kumar and the other under Assistant Commandant Gufran Ahmad, supported by a small local police element. Both teams moved from Bhaluahi camp under the cover of darkness, carefully avoiding Maoist surveillance networks. After a full day of combing without contact, they halted at a vantage point, where their vigilance paid off. Around 1715 hrs, smoke rising from a nearby hillock suggested Maoist activity. Recognising the opportunity, Assistant Commandant Chandan Kumar silently coordinated a three-directional approach, with Constable Mishra advancing in the south-west element. As the troops ascended toward the suspected site in fading light, the Maoists detected movement and unleashed heavy fire. Despite the sudden threat and the wounding of Head Constable Nagendra Prasad, the assault continued. During the charge, Constable Mishra and his commander confronted a sentry position at close range. The Maoists attempted to escape while firing indiscriminately, but in a bold and rapid counter-move, both troopers closed the distance and neutralised them. Maoist fire intensified, including grenade attacks, yet Constable Mishra remained composed, advancing further under extremely limited cover. When two Maoists attempted to break out toward their position while firing, Mishra and his commander reacted instantly. They moved laterally, engaged the fleeing militants at close quarters, and inflicted injuries that forced them back into the jungle. The firefight continued until darkness set in. A search at first light revealed four Maoists killed, including senior regional and zonal commanders, along with significant weapons and equipment. Constable Amarnath Mishra’s conduct during the operation reflected exceptional courage, steadfastness, and an unflinching commitment to duty in a highly volatile combat environment.

Name: Syed Ali Usam
Biography: Major Syed Ali Usman of 8 Assam, son of Syed Mohmead Ali and Mrs. Rehana Ameer, hailed from Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. On 20 February 1998, based on information about a hideout of houses in village Kuwariguri in Bodo dominated belt north of Gohpur in Assam, Major Syed Ali Usman planned a route along the most difficult approach to ensure cover, concealment and maximum surprise. As his raid group closed in at the suspected group, of houses, Major Syed Ali Usman ordered for a running corden to be laid. While the cordon was being established, the militants opened fire at the column and tried to make their escape. Seeing the militants getting away, the officer with his AK-47 rifle in hip position killed one of them. Subsequent operations led to the elimination of another hardcore militant and recoveries of Arms and Ammunition. Major Syed Ali Usman displayed unparalleled bravery exemplary courage and sterling leadership disregarding threat to his personal safety. Link :https://gallantryawards.gov.in/awardee/330

Name: Hem Singh Rajput
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous)/ 28 February 2005 Naib Subedar Hem Singh Rajput Naib Subedar Hem Singh Rajput served with distinguished honour in the Indian Army as part of the Rajputana Rifles and the 9 Rashtriya Rifles. Born to Shri Hazari Singh and Smt. Kashmiri Devi, he hailed from Alwar and was known for his unwavering dedication, courage, and deep sense of duty toward his comrades and the nation. on 28 February 2005, a team led by Naib Subedar Hem Singh Rajput established contact with terrorists in an intricate triple storey building in Pulwama District in Jammu & Kashmir, where four members of his Ghatak Team were injured. Realising the danger, Naib Subedar Hem Singh Rajput entered the house repeatedly at his own peril to extricate his comrades despite being grievously injured during this act. Unmindful of personal agony, when extricating the last injured comrade, he was involved in a fierce face-to-face encounter with four terrorists. He was again hit by a volley of bullets but displaying exceptional courage, he eliminated one terrorist in a hand-to-hand duel and grievously injured other escaping terrorists before making the supreme sacrifice. Naib Subedar Hem Singh Rajput, thus, displayed conspicuous gallantry and bravery beyond compare, concern for fellow comrades and made the supreme sacrifice in the highest traditions of the Indian Army.

Name: CHANDAN KUMAR
Biography: Shri Chandan Kumar, serving as an Assistant Commandant with 205 CoBRA, played an important role during the January 2016 operation in the Aurangabad-Gaya belt, demonstrating these qualities with exceptional clarity. Acting on intelligence inputs indicating the presence of Maoist cadres across the forested stretches of Bhaluahi, Gopaldera, Morma, Kachnar, Chhuchiya, and Dulare, the operation was carefully conceptualised by Commandant Rabish Kumar Singh. To maintain secrecy and surprise, only two small, highly mobile teams one led by Shri Chandan Kumar and the other by Assistant Commandant Gufran Ahmad were launched on 7 January 2016, supported by a limited police component. Under the cover of thick vegetation and darkness, the teams bypassed Maoist early-warning systems and moved deep into the forest. Although no contact was made during the day’s search, both teams halted at advantageous ground to observe the area. Their patience paid off. Around 1715 hrs, smoke rising from a nearby hillock indicated possible Maoist activity. Shri Chandan Kumar quickly assembled his junior commanders through silent signals and devised a three-pronged encirclement. While the northern and southern flanks were secured by the second team, he personally led a group of troopers from the south-west, mindful that fading daylight increased the risk of Maoists escaping. As anticipated, Maoists opened sudden heavy fire as his team advanced. Undeterred by this imminent danger, Shri Chandan Kumar pressed forward. One of his men, Head Constable Nagendra Prasad, was wounded early in the advance, yet he signalled the team to continue moving. Closing in on a sentry post, he and Constable Amarnath Mishra confronted two Maoists at close range. Despite intense fire and grenade blasts, they charged forward and neutralised both. As additional Maoist groups attempted to flee under covering fire, Shri Chandan Kumar o rdered reinforcement teams to close in while he and his buddy continued advancing under minimal cover. In another close encounter, they engaged two fleeing Maoists, injuring them and forcing them back into the jungle. At first light the next morning, a detailed search revealed four dead Maoists, including senior regional and zonal commanders, along with a substantial cache of weapons, explosives, and communication equipment. Through his decisive leadership, exceptional courage, and unyielding commitment to duty, Shri Chandan Kumar exemplified the highest professional standards of CoBRA operations.

Name: AMIT DAHIYA
Unit: First Battalion the Parachute Regiment (Special Force)
Citation Details: 28 July 2021 to 01 August 2021 Major Amit Dahiya, Sena Medal was leading a Search and Destroy Operation Team tasked to eliminate foreign terrorists in Pulwama district based on the intelligence provided by General Officer Commanding, Counter Insurgency Force (Victor) and corroborated by different intelligence agencies. The officer through his meticulous planning and tactical acumen inducted his Team in general area under inclement weather conditions using unexpected route to achieve complete surprise. He astutely deployed his Sniper Detachments to observe the area from vantage points and stops to cut off likely escape routes. At 0605 hours, civilian movement was seen in the general area. Terrorists upon sensing danger came out from a Dhok and started firing indiscriminately using civilians as cover. On ascertaining threat to own troops and civilians, Major Amit Dahiya, Sena Medal displayed bold initiative and tactically maneuvered to close in and neutralized the terrorist in a fierce gun battle. Thereafter, he provided accurate fire support to assist in neutralising second terrorist while ensuring no collateral damage. For displaying enterprising leadership, conspicuous courage, tactical acumen unvanquishable determination, Major Amit Dahiya, Sena Medal is awarded of SHAURYA CHAKRA and

Name: KARN VEER SINGH
Citation Details: 20th October 2021 Based on specific HUMINT regarding movement of two unidentified terrorists in a village in Shopian district (Jammu and Kashmir) an ambush was laid on 20 October 2021. Sepoy Karn Veer Singh was scout of the team which had laid the ambush. At 1030 hours, when intercepted by the ambush, both the terrorists in an attempt to escape jumped into a nalla. Sepoy Karn Veer Singh foreseeing the contingency of terrorists escape dashed after them alone for 100 meters. Terrorists realizing that they were being chased fired at him indiscriminately and lobbed grenades injuring him. Undaunted by his injuries, Sepoy Karn Veer Singh crawled ahead for 30 meters and accurately engaged the terrorists and pinned them down. Valorous at close range, he eliminated terrorist in an intense firefight. Displaying unprecedented courage and devotion to duty Sepoy Karn Veer Singh continued to engage the second terrorist, injured him before receiving a bullet injury on his head, and laid his life in the line of duty. For eliminating one hardcore terrorist and injuring another one, despite being mortally wounded, Sepoy Karn Veer Singh is awarded of SHAURYA CHAKRA (POSTHUMOUS)

Name: MADHU SOODHANAN PILLAI KG
Biography: Shaurya Chakra/ 05 June 1984 Nk Madhusoodanan Pillai of a Company of a MADRAS Battalion was engaged in the Operation against extremists holding strong points in and around the Golden Temple, Amritsar. His company was given the task of clearing the extremists from the southern Parikrama area. The Company wqas to move forward after the leading company, the another company, had established a foothold on the ground floor of Parikrama. However, as the Operation was getting delayed because of effective hold-ups enroute, company had to proceed closely behind the leading company, the company had thus to fight through to reach the heavy fire from Light Machine Guns from extremists in the towers. At a critical juncture, Naik Madhusoodanan Pillair rushed forward and cleared the nearest Light Machine Gun after a close quarter battle in which he sustained injuries. His bravery helped the company in clearing the extremists from the southern Parikrama area. Naik Madhusoodanan Pillai was awarded Shaurya Chakra.

Name: MOHANAN PAPPINI VEETIL
Biography: Shaurya Chakra/ 12 April 1983 Major Mohanan Pappini Veetil was the 2IC of MADRAS bn which was inducted in Mon district of Nagaland in February 1981. Major Mohanan was directed to establish an effective intelligence net work to show the civil populace the sincerity of the Security Force in wanting to assist the locals and to win over their hearts and minds. He moved fearlessly from village to village, house to house, in a spirited effort to woo the masses and win their confidence. On 12 April 1983, one of the sources of Major Mohanan brought information that some undergrounds were going towards Shengha Tangten for exfiltration. Immediately, a special Operation was launched to apprehend the individuals. Major Mohanan was in charge of the columns operating from Mon. While moving on the tract Shengha Tangten to Shengha Chingnyu he saw the under grounds and immediately ordered his column and that of Captain Subroto Mitra to rush and apprehend them alive. The undergrounds fled and ran into the thick jungles in small groups. The officer, though in low medical category, rushed towards the escaping hostiles through thick jungle, cut off their routes of get away by outflanking them, and with utter disregard for his personal safety, personally overpowered two of the three undergrounds who were trying to flee. Inspired by his bold and courageous action, his men pressed home the charge and captured all the eleven fleeing hostiles alive. This led to a further apprehension of more undergrounds including a notorious and the most wanted man of the undergrounds, Mr Noktu Konyak Ranapeyo and his aide, SS Private Khatwant Konyak. His act of gallantry in apprehending the undergrounds set an example for others to emulate. For this tremendous zeal, dedication, and devotion to duty of a most exceptional order and outstanding courage, Maj Mohanan Pappini Veetil received the award of Shaurya Chakra.

Name: INDERJEET SINGH
Biography: Major Inderjeet Singh of the 34 Rashtriya Rifles, son of Shri Manmohan Singh and Smt. Parmjit Kaur, hails from Pune in Maharashtra. On 03 February 1998 Major Inderjeet Singh moved his company at, midnight to cordon village Chak Dewan Lachhmandas in Badgam District, Jammu and Kashmir. During the search he detected an underground stronghold of the militants. When probed, the militants opened indiscriminate fire on the search party. Undeterred the officer immediately cordoned off the entire group of bourn to prevent the militants escape. At 1330 hours a militant attempted to escape under cover of heavy fire. Major Inderjeet Singh putting his own life at a grave risk of his life spontaneously accousted him and shot him dead at close quarters. Another militant, when spotted at 1800 hours in another building, engaged the search party with sophisticatad grenade launcher and automatic fire. Sensing his desperation and the approaching darkness, Major lnderjeet Singh exhibiting courage beyond the call of duty, closed in with the house with total contempt for the flying lead. Judging the position of the militant accurately he kicked open the door, exposing himself perilously, and shot the militant dead in a flash with precision. Major Inderjeet Singh, thus, led his company bravely and brought the operation to a logical and successful conclusion. Link :https://gallantryawards.gov.in/awardee/309

Name: MALUK CHAND
Biography: Lance Naik Maluk Chand of 16 Dogra Regiment was part of a search and destroy mission launched with a small team in the Swan area of Jammu and Kashmir on 10 May 1999. During the operation, the column came under intense fire from well-entrenched militants, leaving all ranks exposed in open ground under heavy fire. With exceptional alertness and courage, he immediately brought his Light Machine Gun into action, preventing a potential disaster. Despite being in full view of the militants and under continuous fire, he held his ground and kept engaging the enemy with accurate bursts. When a bullet struck him in the throat, he refused to withdraw, continuing to fire until his comrades were able to reposition. Grievously wounded and bleeding, he then charged towards the militants, killing one in close combat and, even in his dying moments, indicated the direction of escape of the last militant. For his conspicuous gallantry, devotion to duty, and supreme sacrifice, Lance Naik Maluk Chand was awarded the Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous).

Name: ANUJ SOOD
Biography: Major Anuj Sood, served as a Company Commander with 21 Rashtriya Rifles in Kupwara district, Jammu & Kashmir, and was engaged in counter-insurgency operations. Between 29 April and 03 May 2020, he was involved in a critical sequence of actions that ultimately demonstrated his unwavering courage and commitment to protecting civilian lives. On 01 May 2020, after receiving precise intelligence about the presence of two terrorists in the Watsar Forest, Major Sood quickly initiated an operation to intercept them. When the terrorists were sighted, they responded with indiscriminate gunfire before attempting to escape. Major Sood and his team returned controlled fire, preventing civilian casualties despite the hostile situation. The following day, 02 May 2020, the terrorists were traced again to a location in Chanjimula. Recognising the threat posed to civilians being held hostage, Major Sood personally joined the assault team consisting of the Commanding Officer and three other soldiers. With complete disregard for his own safety, he advanced into the target house under heavy fire. His resolute actions helped secure the release of three civilians. In an effort to rescue the remaining two hostages, he physically engaged one of the terrorists inside the structure. During this intense encounter, he sustained multiple gunshot wounds while ensuring the safety of the civilians. For his remarkable bravery, supreme sacrifice, and steadfast dedication to duty, Major Anuj Sood was posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra.

Name: DEEPAK KUMAR PADDA
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous)/ 23 May 2005 Major Deepak Kumar Padda was born on 30 January 1976 in Hoshiarpur district in Punjab to Lieutenant Colonel Paras Ram, an army veteran and Smt Sharda Rani.1 He did his initial schooling from Kendriya Vidyalaya, Pathankot and later did his Bachelors in Science from DAV College, Chandigarh. Since his childhood Major Deepak Kumar Padda wanted to serve in the Armed Forces. He joined the Indian Army at the age of 23 after his training from the Indian Military Academy (IMA), Dehradun. Major Deepak Padda was commissioned in the 85 Armoured Regiment on 13 May 2000 at Mamun. He served with his parent unit for four years, and took part in various challenging operations. While in service he married Ms. Sonia Padda, and later they were blessed with a son Ritviek. Major Deepak Kumar Padda during his NDA days He was promoted to the rank of Captain in the year 2002, and as a young captain moved to Babina, Jhansi along with its unit in September 2003. He did his instructors course from Armoured Corps Centre and School, Ahmednagar, and later was sent on attachment with 14 GRENADIERS in 2004. He was promoted to the rank of Major in the same year. 85 Armoured Regiment was raised on 01 October 1976 by Late Lt Col DP Singh (Ex 63 CAV and 66 Armd Regt) at Vijay Lines, Ahmednagar. The Regiment on raising was equipped with Vijayanta Tanks. The forbearers of ‘85’ comprised of valiant officers from thirteen Armoured Regiments and gallant men from the Armoured Corps and the Regiment of Artillery. On the other hand, the GRENADIERS is an infantry regiment of the Indian Army with a rich and illustrious history. On 01 October 1943, one of the existing Infantry Division of Eastern Army, the 14 1 @ The GAP team is deeply grateful to Mrs. Sonia Padda for providing us with documents, information, and photographs of Major Deepak Kumar Padda, SC. infantry Division that was located at Chhindwara, was reorganised as training Division to basically hold trained recruits and train them for two months in jungle warfare. For this purpose the Division has raised a few training Battalions. One of its training Battalion, the 34 training Unit was being shared by the GRENADIERS Regimental and 3 MADRAS. Subsequently the MADRAS Regimental started raising its own independent units. 34 Unit was redesignated as 14 BATALLION of the BOMBAY GRENADIERS. After Word War-II was over, the Battalion was de-mobilised on 01 April 1946. The Battalion was re-raised post- independence on 01 January 1965 at Nasirabad, as the 14th Battalion the Grenadiers under Major SRS Manhas. The battalion has participated in many operations since its raising including OP Rakshak from October 1994-May 1997 and from October 1998- May 1999. The battalion was again part of Operation Rakshak from July 2004- September 2007. Major Deepak Kumar Padda and Mrs Sonia Padda Kashmir Insurgency Pakistan has been, since independence, aiding and abetting terrorism in the state of Jammu and Kashmir. The role Indian Army is mandated to safeguard National Interests from External Aggression and Internal Subversion. The Indian Army is committed to bringing down the levels of violence to "manageable levels" in Jammu and Kashmir so as to restore the confidence of the people and create a secure environment to facilitate smooth governance and socio economic development. Army’s focus is on conducting of surgical and professional operations based on hard intelligence, while cause minimum inconvenience to the local populace. Simultaneously, the focus has been on destruction of terrorist infrastructure, resulting in a large number of hideouts being busted and recovery of huge caches of arms and ammunition. The Indian Army today is engaged in the management of complex and active land borders coupled with ongoing Counter Insurgency (CI)/ Counter Terrorism (CT) operations leading to a ‘No War No Peace’ Scenario. The primary role of the Indian Army is to preserve National interests and safeguard sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of India against external threats and internal subversion by deterrence or by waging war. Additionally, the Army is also geared to provide assistance to civil authority when required. Major Deepak Kumar Padda By 2005, Major Deepak Kumar Padda had put in around 05 years of service and had gained the fieldcraft skills required to be operation-ready officer. The same year, there were a discernible drop in infiltration from Pakistan since 2004. The assessed successful infiltration up to December 2005 had come down to 335. This reduction was because of counter measures adopted by the Army. However, the period during June - July 2005 witnessed an upsurge in infiltration attempts by terrorists, belying the claims by Pakistan of their efforts in curbing terrorism from their soil. The residual strength of the terrorists as well as their potential, in terms of weapons and related infrastructure shown a decline, placing the terrorists on the backfoot. The Army's strategy of 'Iron Fist in a Velvet Glove' paid rich dividends, since it focused on conduct of surgical and professional operations based on real time intelligence, which causes minimum inconvenience to the local populace.2 During the year 2005, 1,990 terrorist incidents occurred as compared to 2,565 incidents during the year 2004. 557 civilians were killed in the year 2005, compared to 707 last year. The number of Security Force personnel killed in the year 2005 was 189, compared to 281 in 2004. 917 terrorists were killed in the year 2005, compared to 976 during the previous year. 3 It was in the Kupwara district, which according under section 3 of the Armed Forces (Jammu & Kashmir) Special Powers Act, 1990 was notified as ‘disturbed’ area, where Major Deepak Kumar Padda was posted on attachment with 14 GRENADIERS during the operation Rakshak in 2005. Major Deepak Kumar Padda was commanding the A’coy of 14 Grenadier and the Company Operating Base was on Tangdhar road. Major Deepak Kumar Padda was the commander of the A’coy that executed an operation on 23 May 2005 in general area Rangwar, District Kupwara, Jammu & Kashmir. On receipt of an information, Major Deepak rushed to the target site. Displaying acute tactical acumen, he readjusted the team positions to counter the disadvantageous terrain and himself crawled ahead to effectively engage the terrorists. In the intense fire-fight, Commander of the neighbouring team got injured. To prevent his men sustain further scathing bullets, Major Deepak charged firing on to the terrorists. Unprepared, for this kind of bravery and ferociousness, the terrorists started firing indiscriminately, hitting Major Deepak in his abdomen. Meanwhile, Commander of one of the teams sustained a fatal injury as he eliminated one of the terrorists. Unable to accept this irreparable loss. Major Deepak crawled ahead, ignoring his near fatal bullet injury and exhibiting unprecedented gumption, fatally killed the second terrorist with effective fire. Major Padda was evacuated from the site of action, and later succumbed to his injuries on 04 June 2005 in Army Hospital. Major Deepak Kumar Padda is survived by his wife Mrs Sonia Padda and son Ritviek. A school in Daulatpur, Pathankot, Punjab has been named as Shaheed Major Deepak Kumar Padda Government Senior Secondary School in his honour. Name: P TRINADHA RAO
Biography: Assistant Assault Commander P. Trinadha Rao, serving with the Greyhounds, demonstrated notable proficiency in counter-insurgency operations during the major engagement in the Andhra-Odisha Border (AOB) region in October 2016. Acting on credible intelligence that a large concentration of AOBSZC Maoists had assembled in the cut-off region with intent to initiate violence, three assault units of the Greyhounds, supported by local police and SIB personnel, were deployed on the evening of 23 October 2016. The teams undertook an arduous overnight march of over 26 km, traversing hostile terrain, landmine-prone areas, and Maoist strongholds before reaching the outskirts of Ramgurha village by dawn on 24 October. As one commando group moved into the forested hills north of the village, they were detected and immediately engaged by Maoist sentries using automatic and semi-automatic weapons. Despite sustained hostile fire, the Greyhounds advanced and neutralised two Maoists, thereafter pursuing a group of 60–70 armed cadres. AAC Trinadha Rao, leading a small element, crossed a Nala under intense enemy fire and intercepted a contingent of 20–25 Maoists attempting to move toward Ramgurha. Forcing them back toward a hillock, he and his team faced a prolonged barrage of gunfire and grenades from militants occupying dominant ground. Although injured by bullets, he remained resolute, urging his men to advance. Moving cover-to-cover, he led a flank assault on the boulder-held position and successfully neutralised the Maoists firing from it. His sub-group ultimately eliminated three Maoist cadres identified later as a Special Zonal Committee Member, a District Committee Member, and an Area Committee Member and recovered an AK-47 rifle, an SLR, and a pistol. His decisive action enabled other commandos to reorganise, seal escape routes, and sustain pressure on the fleeing militants. AAC Trinadha Rao’s leadership, personal example, and steadfast courage under extreme danger played a pivotal role in preventing a mass escape and ensuring the success of the operation, an achievement far beyond normal expectations of duty.

Biography: Shaurya Chakra/ 05 June 1984 Nk Madhusoodanan Pillai of a Company of a MADRAS Battalion was engaged in the Operation against extremists holding strong points in and around the Golden Temple, Amritsar. However, as the Operation was getting delayed because of effective hold-ups enroute, company had to proceed closely behind the leading company, the company had thus to fight through to reach the heavy fire from Light Machine Guns from extremists in the towers. At a critical juncture, Naik Madhusoodanan Pillair rushed forward and cleared the nearest Light Machine Gun after a close quarter battle in which he sustained injuries. His bravery helped the company in clearing the extremists from the southern Parikrama area. Naik Madhusoodanan Pillai was awarded Shaurya Chakra.

Name: MOHANAN PAPPINI VEETIL
Biography: Shaurya Chakra/ 12 April 1983 Major Mohanan Pappini Veetil was the 2IC of MADRAS bn which was inducted in Mon district of Nagaland in February 1981. Major Mohanan was directed to establish an effective intelligence net work to show the civil populace the sincerity of the Security Force in wanting to assist the locals and to win over their hearts and minds. He moved fearlessly from village to village, house to house, in a spirited effort to woo the masses and win their confidence. On 12 April 1983, one of the sources of Major Mohanan brought information that some undergrounds were going towards Shengha Tangten for exfiltration. Immediately, a special Operation was launched to apprehend the individuals. Major Mohanan was in charge of the columns operating from Mon. While moving on the tract Shengha Tangten to Shengha Chingnyu he saw the under grounds and immediately ordered his column and that of Captain Subroto Mitra to rush and apprehend them alive. The undergrounds fled and ran into the thick jungles in small groups. The officer, though in low medical category, rushed towards the escaping hostiles through thick jungle, cut off their routes of get away by outflanking them, and with utter disregard for his personal safety, personally overpowered two of the three undergrounds who were trying to flee. Inspired by his bold and courageous action, his men pressed home the charge and captured all the eleven fleeing hostiles alive. This led to a further apprehension of more undergrounds including a notorious and the most wanted man of the undergrounds, Mr Noktu Konyak Ranapeyo and his aide, SS Private Khatwant Konyak. His act of gallantry in apprehending the undergrounds set an example for others to emulate. For this tremendous zeal, dedication, and devotion to duty of a most exceptional order and outstanding courage, Maj Mohanan Pappini Veetil received the award of Shaurya Chakra.

Name: DEWAN SINGH
Biography: The UN Peacekeeping mission in Gaza was an attempt to resolve the of Arab-Israel conflict after the Arab-Israel war of 1956. This was the first mission for which the UN security council authorized the deployment of armed military contingents along with the UN Emergency force. The United Nations Emergency Force was assigned the duty of maintaining a ceasefire India was among the top contributors to the UNEF, from November 1956 to May 1967, eleven Indian infantry battalions served successively with this force. The officers of Indian army Major General P S Gyani and Brigadier I J Rikhye were force commanders for this UN Mission. The highly regarded platoon of the 3 PARA (KUMAON) [Now 3 PARA (SF)] was engaged in clearing the minefields. Havildar Dewan Singh, while obeying the command of his commander, displayed commendable gallant and courage by accounting to several plastic anti-tank and anti-personnel mines. Havildar Dewan Singh being no.1 leading man of the 1st mine lifting party, along with Naik Puran Chand while prodding for mines got exposed to a massive mine explosion. An Anti-personnel plastic mine got activated and went off very near to him and he got severely injured and received shrapnel wounds in many parts of his body. Despite being severely wounded and with negligible visibility, due to dense clouds of dust, his duty spurred him to continue to lead his party by personally going forward to assist Naik Puran Chand to neutralize the 18th anti-tank mine of the day. The mine, however, exploded blowing up both Havildar Dewan Singh and Naik Puran Chand. Havildar Dewan Singh and his sacrifice have made him an integral part of the Indian Army’s glorious history. This act made him an eternal source of inspiration for the generations to come. For his undiminishing dedication and resilience, Havildar Dewan Singh received for his duty Ashoka Chakra CL-III (now Shaurya Chakra).
Citation Details: No. 1138887 Havildar Dewan Singh, 3 Bn The Para Regt. (Kumaon) (Posthumous) (10th April, 1957) On 10th April, 1957, Havildar Dewan Singh while serving with the United Nations Emergency Force in Sinai and Gaza Strip was leading No. 1 mine lifting party with Naik Puran Chand and accounted for 17 plastic anti - tank mines and several anti-personnel mines. Although suffering from fatigue he refused to fall back in the absence of experienced relief in plastic mine lifting. While Naik Puran Chand and his party were prodding the mines, an antipersonnel mine went off at a distance of five yards and severely wounded Havildar Dewan Singh. In Spite of this, his sense of duty spurred him to continue to lead his party by personally going forward to assist Naik Puran Chand neutralise the 18th anti-tank mine of the day. The mine, however, exploded blowing up both Havildar Dewan Singh and Naik Puran Chand. Havildar Dewan Singh set a fine example of leadership and personal courage. He sacrificed his life in the performance of his duty. Throughout the operations none of his men were involved in any accident and he was personally responsible for neutralising several anti-tank mines which needed skilled engineering experience, Havildar Dewan Singh’s supreme sacrifice in the cause of his duty has set a fine example in the best traditions of our army.

Name: CHANDRA SINGH
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous)/ 25 November 2016 Naik Chandra Singh In November 2016, Naik Chandra Singh was deployed as part of a stop group during a Cordon and Search Operation in a village in Sopore district, Jammu and Kashmir. The target was a house sheltering two armed militants. During the operation, the militants opened heavy fire and hurled grenades in an attempt to break the security cordon and escape. One of the militants charged directly toward Naik Chandra Singh’s position, firing his weapon. In the ensuing gunfight, Naik Chandra Singh sustained grievous abdominal injuries. Despite his critical condition, he displayed exceptional courage and continued to engage the militant, understanding the imminent threat posed to his fellow soldiers. With unwavering determination and disregard for his own life, Naik Chandra Singh successfully neutralised the militant at close range, preventing a potential breakout and saving the lives of his comrades. He later succumbed to his injuries at the operation site. For his extraordinary bravery, presence of mind, and supreme sacrifice in the line of duty, Naik Chandra Singh was posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra.

Name: VARSI VASUDEV RAO
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous) / 13 August 1994 https://gallantryawards.gov.in/awardee/2198 On 13th August 1994 in a village in Thoubal district in Manipur, a column was tasked to seek and destroy Naga militants. Naik Rao was leader of the leading section, when they reached the village, they were fired upon by the militants hiding in the college complex. Naik Rao and his men returned the fire. However, he was hit by a bullet in his chest, Bleeding profusely he led his men with extreme courage and total disregard to his own safety, till he breathed his last, This supreme sacrifice of his galvanized his column into action and the operation resulted in subsequent killing of nine militants and apprehension of one of them. Naik Varsi Vasudev Rao, displayed exemplary courage, firm determination and devotion to duty at the cost of his own life.

Name: DHARAM SINGH
Biography: Subedar Dharam Singh, was recruited in the 5 MAHAR and was deployed in the United Nations Mission in Somalia (UNOSOM-II) in 1993. The Mahar regiment has a long and proud tradition of bearing arms. Although the regiment was initially intended to be manned by the members from the Mahar community, today it is one of the most diverse regiments in the Indian Army. In the 19th century, they were recruited by the British East India Company and were part of the Company’s Bombay Army. However, with the introduction of the ‘class regiments’ policy after the First War of Independence of 1857, the British government demobilised the Mahar troops. When the First World War broke out in 1914, the British government was forced to expand its recruiting policies and a Mahar battalion was raised in 1917. After the war ended, the battalion was disbanded again in March 1921. In 1941, when Dr BR Ambedkar was appointed to the Viceroy’s Executive Council, he influenced the British government to enlist the Mahar troops into the army. In October 1941, 1 MAHAR was raised in Belgaum, thus establishing the origin of the present-day Mahar Regiment. Between the two wars, the demand to raise Mahar regiment was constantly raised. The United Nations (UN) initiated two peacekeeping missions in Somalia to deal with the inter-clan conflict that had continued for decades. Somalia (then Somaliland) was under the colonial rule of Britain and Italy. On 1 July 1960, two divisions of Somalia were merged together to form the Somalia Republic. Soon after independence it descended into inter-clan conflict and the country was in a state of chaos. The UN volunteers were working in Somalia providing humanitarian aid, even before the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) Resolution 733 (1992) was passed. This resolution urged the concerned parties in Somalia to end all hostilities promote reconciliation and facilitate delivery of humanitarian assistance. On 24 April 1992, under UNSC Resolution 751 (1992), the first UN mission in Somalia (UNOSOM-I) was launched. During UNOSOM-I, an Indian Naval Task Force was deployed to aid the United States of America (USA) led United Task Force (UNITAF). However, due to the persistent attack from the armed rebels, on 26 March 1993, UNSC Resolution 814 (1993) was passed establishing UNOSOM-II. Under this resolution, immediate deployment of forces to end all violence was made, primarily focusing on disarmament of armed groups and rebuilding the Somalia society among others. Subedar Dharam Singh of 5 MAHAR, was part of an escort party, with Number 2 Irish Army Transport Company logistics convoy, which was moving from Mogadishu to Baidoa. The vehicle was ambushed by the militiamen and Subedar Dharam Singh and his party were caught amidst the fire fight and pinned down by it. While he shot a militiaman down and was preparing to target another four, he found that his magazine became empty. Showing quick reflexes and thinking he threw a stun grenade at the militiamen. His quick thinking paid off as the grenade unnerved the militiamen and he was able to put one of them down and was able to seize his G3A3 automatic rifle. He later assaulted from a flank under the cover fire of light machine gun (LMG) and was successful in capturing two more militiamen alive. For his gallantry and devotion to his duty, he was awarded Shaurya Chakra on 15 March 1994.

Name: SANJAY KAUSHIK
Biography: Shaurya Chakra / 01 July 2009 On 01 July 2009 at 1300h, IC-46936F Lieutenant Colonel Sanjay Kaushik leading the Battalion Ghatak column, moved on reliable input about presence of four terrorists in house of a suspect at village Nilsu. On spot interrogation, provided input that the terrorists were likely to be hiding in the adjoining forest. The officer displayed tactical acumen by immediately resisting the cordon and coordinating a two pronged probe to locate terrorists in the forest which had dense foliage and steep slopes. On being probed, the terrorists fired on own parties spread along a nala, covered with big boulders and dense foliage. The fire fight continued in heavy rainstorm for approx two hours, when the officer anticipating approaching fading light, crawled forward from a flank against heavy fire and charged after throwing grenades. Disregarding personal safety, he closed in and killed two terrorists from point blank range and facilitated neutralization of the third terrorist. For this act of gallantry, he was awarded Shaurya Chakra on 26 Jan 2010.

Name: CHANDAN KUMAR
Biography: Shri Chandan Kumar, serving as an Assistant Commandant with 205 CoBRA, played an important role during the January 2016 operation in the Aurangabad-Gaya belt, demonstrating these qualities with exceptional clarity. Acting on intelligence inputs indicating the presence of Maoist cadres across the forested stretches of Bhaluahi, Gopaldera, Morma, Kachnar, Chhuchiya, and Dulare, the operation was carefully conceptualised by Commandant Rabish Kumar Singh. To maintain secrecy and surprise, only two small, highly mobile teams one led by Shri Chandan Kumar and the other by Assistant Commandant Gufran Ahmad were launched on 7 January 2016, supported by a limited police component. Under the cover of thick vegetation and darkness, the teams bypassed Maoist early-warning systems and moved deep into the forest. Although no contact was made during the day’s search, both teams halted at advantageous ground to observe the area. Their patience paid off. Around 1715 hrs, smoke rising from a nearby hillock indicated possible Maoist activity. Shri Chandan Kumar quickly assembled his junior commanders through silent signals and devised a three-pronged encirclement. While the northern and southern flanks were secured by the second team, he personally led a group of troopers from the south-west, mindful that fading daylight increased the risk of Maoists escaping. As anticipated, Maoists opened sudden heavy fire as his team advanced. Undeterred by this imminent danger, Shri Chandan Kumar pressed forward. One of his men, Head Constable Nagendra Prasad, was wounded early in the advance, yet he signalled the team to continue moving. Closing in on a sentry post, he and Constable Amarnath Mishra confronted two Maoists at close range. Despite intense fire and grenade blasts, they charged forward and neutralised both. As additional Maoist groups attempted to flee under covering fire, Shri Chandan Kumar o rdered reinforcement teams to close in while he and his buddy continued advancing under minimal cover. In another close encounter, they engaged two fleeing Maoists, injuring them and forcing them back into the jungle. At first light the next morning, a detailed search revealed four dead Maoists, including senior regional and zonal commanders, along with a substantial cache of weapons, explosives, and communication equipment. Through his decisive leadership, exceptional courage, and unyielding commitment to duty, Shri Chandan Kumar exemplified the highest professional standards of CoBRA operations.

Name: AMIT DAHIYA
Unit: First Battalion the Parachute Regiment (Special Force)
Citation Details: 28 July 2021 to 01 August 2021 Major Amit Dahiya, Sena Medal was leading a Search and Destroy Operation Team tasked to eliminate foreign terrorists in Pulwama district based on the intelligence provided by General Officer Commanding, Counter Insurgency Force (Victor) and corroborated by different intelligence agencies. The officer through his meticulous planning and tactical acumen inducted his Team in general area under inclement weather conditions using unexpected route to achieve complete surprise. He astutely deployed his Sniper Detachments to observe the area from vantage points and stops to cut off likely escape routes. At 0605 hours, civilian movement was seen in the general area. Terrorists upon sensing danger came out from a Dhok and started firing indiscriminately using civilians as cover. On ascertaining threat to own troops and civilians, Major Amit Dahiya, Sena Medal displayed bold initiative and tactically maneuvered to close in and neutralized the terrorist in a fierce gun battle. Thereafter, he provided accurate fire support to assist in neutralising second terrorist while ensuring no collateral damage. For displaying enterprising leadership, conspicuous courage, tactical acumen unvanquishable determination, Major Amit Dahiya, Sena Medal is awarded of SHAURYA CHAKRA and

Name: MALUK CHAND
Biography: Lance Naik Maluk Chand of 16 Dogra Regiment was part of a search and destroy mission launched with a small team in the Swan area of Jammu and Kashmir on 10 May 1999. During the operation, the column came under intense fire from well-entrenched militants, leaving all ranks exposed in open ground under heavy fire. With exceptional alertness and courage, he immediately brought his Light Machine Gun into action, preventing a potential disaster. Despite being in full view of the militants and under continuous fire, he held his ground and kept engaging the enemy with accurate bursts. When a bullet struck him in the throat, he refused to withdraw, continuing to fire until his comrades were able to reposition. Grievously wounded and bleeding, he then charged towards the militants, killing one in close combat and, even in his dying moments, indicated the direction of escape of the last militant. For his conspicuous gallantry, devotion to duty, and supreme sacrifice, Lance Naik Maluk Chand was awarded the Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous).

Name: ANUJ SOOD
Biography: Major Anuj Sood, served as a Company Commander with 21 Rashtriya Rifles in Kupwara district, Jammu & Kashmir, and was engaged in counter-insurgency operations. Between 29 April and 03 May 2020, he was involved in a critical sequence of actions that ultimately demonstrated his unwavering courage and commitment to protecting civilian lives. On 01 May 2020, after receiving precise intelligence about the presence of two terrorists in the Watsar Forest, Major Sood quickly initiated an operation to intercept them. When the terrorists were sighted, they responded with indiscriminate gunfire before attempting to escape. Major Sood and his team returned controlled fire, preventing civilian casualties despite the hostile situation. The following day, 02 May 2020, the terrorists were traced again to a location in Chanjimula. Recognising the threat posed to civilians being held hostage, Major Sood personally joined the assault team consisting of the Commanding Officer and three other soldiers. With complete disregard for his own safety, he advanced into the target house under heavy fire. His resolute actions helped secure the release of three civilians. In an effort to rescue the remaining two hostages, he physically engaged one of the terrorists inside the structure. During this intense encounter, he sustained multiple gunshot wounds while ensuring the safety of the civilians. For his remarkable bravery, supreme sacrifice, and steadfast dedication to duty, Major Anuj Sood was posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra.

Name: SATISH DAHIYA
Biography: Shaurya Chakra (Posthumous)/ 14 February 2017 Major Satish Dahiya Major Satish Dahiya, a braveheart of the Indian Army, hailed from Banihari village in Mahendragarh district of Haryana. Born on 22 September 1985 to Shri Achal Singh Dahiya and Smt Anita Devi, he was the only child of his parents. He completed his schooling in Uttar Pradesh and pursued higher education from Rajasthan University before fulfilling his dream of joining the Indian Army. Commissioned into the Army Service Corps on 12 December 2009, he began his career in logistics but soon distinguished himself in field duties. His first posting was with 1 Naga Battalion at Nowgam in Jammu & Kashmir, where he actively participated in counterinsurgency operations and went on to become the Ghatak Platoon Commander. In 2012, he married Ms. Sujata of Pawera village in Mahendragarh, and the couple was blessed with a daughter, Priyasha, in April 2015. After serving with the 539 ASC Battalion, he was deputed to 30 Rashtriya Rifles, a unit actively engaged in counter-insurgency operations in J&K. Known for his exceptional leadership and courage, Maj Dahiya was respected as an officer who always led from the front. On 14 February 2017, acting on specific intelligence about the presence of militants in Hajin Kralgund village of Kupwara district, a joint operation was launched by the 30 RR battalion and J&K Police. Major Dahiya led one of the assault teams in the inner cordon, while the outer cordon was led by his Commanding Officer. As the troops approached the suspected house, the terrorists opened heavy fire. Showing tactical acumen and courage, Maj Dahiya maneuvered his men to block escape routes. Despite being shot and seriously wounded in the ensuing firefight, he continued to engage the terrorists, even requesting evacuation for his injured comrades while refusing aid for himself. He successfully neutralized one terrorist before eventually succumbing to his injuries after being evacuated to 92 Base Hospital. For his extraordinary bravery, leadership under fire, and supreme sacrifice, Major Satish Dahiya was posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra

Name: M LAKSHMANAN
Biography: Shaurya Chakra/ 26 January 1962 On 14 July 1961, at about 10 AM No 2543883 Lance Naik M Lakshmanan, who was working in the Officers Mess on the banks of the river Jhelum, heard a scream for help from two Other Ranks in the river. They had been carried away by the swift current to the middle of the river some 60 feet from the bank. Without any slightest hesitation and in complete disregard of the life, Lance Naik Lakshmanan rushed instantly to the aid of the two drowning men. He managed to get hold of them and started bringing them back to the river bank. In the process, one of the drowning person caught hold of his foot and dragged him under water. By then he was very nearly exhausted, but did not give up his attempt to rescue the drowning men. He brought both of them to within 20 feet of the river bank, when others, coming to his aid, were able to bring one of them out of the river. He was forced to give up his search only when he was completely exhausted. LNk Lakshmanan showed commendable determination and courage beyond the call of duty in going to the aid of two drowning men for which he was awarded Shaurya Chakra

Name: PRADEEP BHATIA
Biography: 1 OTHER RECORDS (PHOTO GALLERY) VIDEOS GAZETTE NOTIFICATION/ AUTHORITY Captain Pradeep Bhatia was commissioned into 5 MAHAR and was deployed in the United Nations Mission in Somalia (UNOSOM-II) in 1993.
